item.title: Voters in Israel are deciding whether to oust Netanyahu after 3 years of war
item.description: JERUSALEM — Israelis are voting in a pivotal election Tuesday as their country wrestles with unresolved wars, continues to reel from Hamas' 2023 attack and is deeply divided over the character of the state and the right person to lead it. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who voted just after midday, faces an array of parties seeking to oust Israel's longest-serving premier from power. Opinion polls have suggested a tight race with his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Over 7 million people are eligible to vote, and tens of thousands have reportedly arrived from overseas. “This is a very moving and fateful moment," Netanyahu said. He told journalists after voting that he believes the Arab parties that could make or break the election" are receiving massive, truly massive, support. They are heading to the polls in unprecedented numbers.” He urged supporters to forget about the beach or the barbecue and vote. More than 31 percent of Israelis voted by noon, the highest voter turnout by midday since 1977, according to figures by the Central Elections Committee. Inside I

item.title: Convenience stores jump on Korea's rice cake dessert boom
item.description: From butter to toppings, Korean rice cakes — called "tteok" — are enjoying a heyday of flavor innovation. As various rice cake desserts lead this year’s food trends, even spawning the term “tteok-run” to refer to lining up before a store opens to secure the trendy treats, convenience store chains are jumping on the bandwagon. According to purchasing data from market research firm Embrain, estimated spending on rice cakes reached 151.9 billion won ($112 million) from September last year to August this year, up 31.2 percent from the previous year. Spending increased by more than 20 percent across all age groups, with purchases by people in their 20s and younger surging 45.5 percent. The rise reflects a growing number of young consumers willing to wait in long lines to try rice cake desserts that have gone viral on social media. item.title: Cold wave advisories take effect across Korea
item.description: Much of Korea will wake up to freezing temperatures Wednesday, as chilly air sweeping in from the northwest brings morning lows below zero in inland areas. Cold wave advisories are in effect across most of the country. Morning temperatures are forecast to range from minus 2 to 7 degrees Celsius nationwide. Parts of northeastern Gyeonggi Province, Gangwon Province, North Chungcheong Province and inland areas of the south are expected to see temperatures dip below freezing, with frost and icy conditions possible in places. Daytime highs will range from 11 to 17 degrees. Forecast lows and highs in major cities are 2 and 13 degrees Celsius in Seoul; 3 and 12 in Incheon; 1 and 13 in Daejeon; 3 and 15 in Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City; 1 and 14 in Daegu; 5 and 15 in Ulsan; and 7 and 17 in Busan. Strong winds will make it feel even colder, particularly in southern parts of the country. The cold spell is expected to last through Thursday, when morning lows will range from minus 1 to 8 degrees and daytime highs from 13 to 18. item.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 10,000 cases as authorities race to slow the spread in African countries
item.description: BUNIA, Congo — The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in Congo has reached 10,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Tuesday, as health authorities race to slow the spread of the disease in multiple African countries . It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and nearly half of the 10,060 confirmed to have the virus have died, according to data from Congo’s Ministry of Health. That also makes it the deadliest outbreak of the disease in the country’s history. The outbreak declared in May is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation. Those obstacles compound the challenge of persuading people to report symptoms and accept care in communities that have endured years of violence and repeated epidemics. On Monday, the official social media account of tvN’s “You Quiz on the Block” shared a preview featuring Shin, accompanied by the caption: “Shin Min-a has consistently donated every year. item.title: 3 ex-officials appeal to top court over 2019 deportation of N. Koreans
item.description: Three former government officials on Tuesday appealed an appellate ruling sentencing them to suspended prison terms for forcibly repatriating two North Korean fishermen in 2019, taking the case to the Supreme Court, sources said. Last week, the Seoul High Court upheld a lower court's guilty verdicts for Chung Eui-yong, former national security adviser; former National Intelligence Service Director Suh Hoon; and former Unification Minister Kim Yeon-chul. All three served in former President Moon Jae-in's administration in November 2019, when Seoul deported two North Korean fishermen back to North Korea after they were captured near the eastern maritime border. The fishermen had been accused of killing 16 fellow crew members on their vessel. A lower court found all three former officials guilty but deferred their sentencing. The appellate court sentenced Chung and Suh to 18 months in prison, suspended for three years, and Kim to a one-year prison term suspended for two years, ruling they violated the basic rights of the fishermen by repatriating them back to their communist homeland. item.title: Citibank Korea appoints new CEO in 1st leadership change in 6 years
item.description: Citibank Korea has appointed Kim Kyoung-ho, its head of corporate banking, as its new CEO, ending a six-year leadership run under his predecessor, the lender said Tuesday. Kim succeeds Yoo Myung-soon, who became the bank’s first female CEO in 2020. He will serve a three-year term. Kim joined Citibank Korea in 2001 and has held a series of senior positions in corporate banking, including large corporate banking and financial institutions coverage, before being promoted to executive vice president in 2021. On Sept. 22, the lender’s executive recommendation committee named him its sole candidate for the top post. His appointment comes as Citi continues to reshape its Korean operations following its exit from consumer banking. With corporate banking now at the core of its local business, Kim’s challenge as an incoming chief will be to build on that strategic shift and ensure its strong performance going forward.

item.title: Instant photo kiosk featuring President Lee set to open at presidential house annex
item.description: An instant four-cut photo kiosk will open at an annex of the presidential house in Seoul, allowing visitors to take photos with images of President Lee Jae Myung, his office said Tuesday. The photo booth will go into service at Sarangchae, a public pavilion annexed to Cheong Wa Dae on Wednesday, marking the first anniversary of Lee's presidency, the presidential office said. Visitors can choose from 32 photo frames featuring Lee; his wife, first lady Kim Hea Kyung; or images of Korean cultural heritage assets before taking photos with them and downloading the photos on their smartphones, according to the office.

item.title: Korea hosts G20 global financial stability conference in Seoul
item.description: Korea's finance ministry on Tuesday hosted a global conference bringing together experts to discuss financial stability and supply chains in the era of artificial intelligence (AI). The Ministry of Finance and Economy and the state-run Korea Development Institute co-hosted the G20 Global Financial Stability Conference 2026 in Seoul, an annual event first held in 2013 to discuss ways to address global financial challenges. Around 300 financial experts from across the globe participated in this year's event, discussing ways to enhance the stability and resilience of the global economy and address risks and challenges arising from AI-driven innovation, according to the ministry. In his opening remarks, Second Vice Finance Minister Huh Chang stressed the spread of AI and the restructuring of supply chains could pose new threats to financial market stability. Huh called for preemptive measures to address AI-related risks and sufficient financial capacity to cope with future turbulence, alongside efforts to link financial safety nets with supply chain resilience. item.title: Foreign tourist arrivals in Korea estimated to have set annual record early
item.description: Foreign tourist arrivals in Korea this year are estimated to have already set an all-time annual record, the culture ministry said Tuesday. Preliminary figures from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism showed that this year's arrivals reached about 18.91 million through Monday, and the total is believed to have surpassed the previous annual record of 18.94 million, set last year, Tuesday, with more than two months left in the year. The ministry expects about 1.94 million people to visit next month if the current trend continues, with the annual total topping 20 million for the first time in the third week of November. Culture, Sports and Tourism Minister Chae Hwi-young said breaking the annual record more than two months early has brought the government's ambitious year-end target of 23 million foreign visitors "within reach." Visitor numbers rose across most major markets, including Chinese-speaking regions, Japan, Southeast Asia, Europe and the Americas. item.title: Kolmar vice chairman confident in K-beauty's continued growth
item.description: Kolmar Group Vice Chairman Yoon Sang-hyun expressed confidence in K-beauty’s continued growth at Amazon Beauty in Seoul 2026 on Tuesday. Yoon delivered a presentation on the sustainability of K-beauty, highlighting the industry's growth potential, driven by the emergence of new brands and an ecosystem connecting product developers with global consumers. Kolmar Korea has served as the event’s exclusive manufacturing sponsor for three consecutive years since its launch in 2024. item.title: No casualties reported in shanty town fire in southern Seoul
item.description: A fire broke out at a shantytown in Seoul's posh southern district of Gangnam on Tuesday, but no casualties have been reported so far, officials said. The fire broke out at about 3:50 p.m. at a makeshift building at Guryong Village, prompting 39 residents to flee to safety, according to fire authorities. Fire authorities issued a Level 1 emergency response at 3:59 p.m. and later raised the response level by one notch as the fire spread. A total of 232 personnel and 70 pieces of equipment were mobilized to the scene to fight the blaze. No injuries or missing persons have been reported so far, and 39 residents have evacuated the area on their own, officials said. Authorities have guided the locals to a safe area and deployed six firefighting helicopters to prevent the blaze from spreading into a wildfire. Firefighting officials plan to look into the cause of the blaze and assess the damage as soon as the blaze is extinguished. The Gangnam Ward office sent a safety text message advising nearby residents to close their windows and for vehicles to avoid the area. President Lee Jae Myung instructe

item.title: S. Korea withdraws 8 diplomatic personnel from Ukraine: FM Cho
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Korea has withdrawn eight diplomatic personnel from Ukraine amid a dispute over Kyiv's disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs). Cho made the remarks during a parliamentary audit of the foreign ministry, saying that despite the partial withdrawal, he has continued communication with the Ukraine foreign minister to resolve the issue. South Korea recalled its ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, earlier this month and decided to withdraw some embassy personnel, citing Kyiv's failure to take steps to resolve the dispute and persistent threats of Russian airstrikes. "Eight have been withdrawn so far," Cho said, adding that the withdrawal had been unavoidable given Ukraine's failure to adequately address the issue. South Korea has demanded an official explanation, an apology and assurances against a recurrence after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly disclosed the transfer of two North Korean soldiers to South Korea during an address to the U.N. item.title: Korean won inches down against US dollar ahead of Fed meeting
item.description: The Korean won edged down against the U.S. dollar Tuesday, as traders have kept a close watch on a Federal Reserve meeting this week. The won was quoted at 1,323.7 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., down 0.6 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. At one point in morning trading, the won advanced to a high of 1,322.8 won per dollar, helped by stronger-than-expected economic growth in the third quarter. The nation's economy grew 1 percent in the July-September period, thanks to semiconductor-led exports and investment. Foreign investors purchased a net 592.9 billion won ($447 million) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index gaining 3.09 percent to close at 5,638.34.

item.title: AMCHAM workshop explores AI-ready workforce, CEO risks
item.description: The American Chamber of Commerce in Korea (AMCHAM) held its HR Workshop 2026 at the Grand Hyatt Seoul on Tuesday, bringing together about 100 business leaders and professionals to discuss artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, workforce transformation and corporate risk management. Under the theme “AI-Ready Workforce: Leading People & Managing Risk in the Age of AI,” the workshop explored how companies can use AI to improve productivity and employee capabilities while addressing legal and organizational challenges. “AI is changing how we work. Our job as leaders is to make that change work for our businesses and our people,” AMCHAM Chairman and CEO James Kim said. “Employees need the skills and confidence to use [AI tools] well, while leaders need to set clear expectations and manage risk.” Rep. item.title: Hanmi Pharm Q3 net income down 69.1% to $10.6 mil.
item.description: Hanmi Pharm on Tuesday reported a third-quarter net income of 14 billion won ($10.6 million), down 69.1 percent from a year earlier. The Korean pharmaceutical company said in a regulatory filing that operating profit for the July-September period fell 31.3 percent on-year to 37.8 billion won. Revenue increased 4.2 percent to 377.4 billion won. The earnings failed to meet market expectations. The average estimate of net profit by analysts stood at 26.5 billion won, according to a survey by Yonhap Infomax, the financial data firm of Yonhap News Agency.

item.title: Ruling party decides to seek parliamentary probe into Supreme Court chief amid impeachment calls
item.description: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) said Tuesday it has decided to seek a parliamentary investigation into Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, with some hardliners calling for his impeachment over allegations of political interference. During a general meeting of its lawmakers, the DPK agreed to push for the probe, aiming to pass a related motion at a parliamentary plenary session scheduled for Thursday next week, DPK floor spokesperson Jeon Eun-su told reporters. The DPK has accused Cho of meddling in last year's presidential election after the Supreme Court overturned a not-guilty verdict in President Lee Jae Myung's election law violation case and sent it back to a lower court for retrial just ahead of the June 3 presidential election. The party also took issue with Cho's refusal to recommend a new candidate for Supreme Court justice as requested by the presidential office, as well as allegations of improper use of official funds. The DPK had previously hinted at seeking Cho's impeachment over the allegations but was also considering seeking a parliamentary investigation i

item.title: Seoul stocks rebound as Anthropic IPO revives AI investment sentiment
item.description: Korean stocks rebounded Tuesday, led by gains in the country’s semiconductor heavyweights, as news of U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic’s planned blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) revived investor appetite after a recent pullback. The benchmark KOSPI opened at 5,658.65, up 3.46 percent from the previous close, according to the Korea Exchange. A buy-sidecar was triggered early in the session at 10:13 a.m., temporarily suspending program buy orders for five minutes after the market’s surge breached the volatility threshold. The index remained in positive territory throughout the session, closing at 5,638.34, up 3.09 percent. Foreign investors and institutions were net buyers of 835.9 billion won ($631.05 million) and 418.5 billion won, respectively, while retail investors sold a net 1. 4 trillion won. item.title: Chip boom fails to lift spending as private consumption falls
item.description: Korea's economy is growing on the back of a semiconductor export boom, but consumers aren't feeling the benefits. Private consumption fell 0.2 percent in the third quarter from the previous quarter, marking its first decline since the second quarter of 2023, according to preliminary data on third quarter economic growth from the Bank of Korea (BOK), Tuesday. Private spending growth had already slowed from 0.6 percent in the first quarter to 0.4 percent in the second before turning negative in the third. Spending declined for both goods, including cars and home appliances, and services, such as financial and dining services. The decline came even as the economy expanded 1 percent in the third quarter from the previous quarter, exceeding the central bank's forecast of 0.3 percent. Weak private spending stood in contrast to stronger headline growth driven by robust semiconductor exports. While the export boom has lifted overall economic growth, its benefits have yet to result in a stronger recovery in domestic consumption. item.title: Bolsonaro's party says it recognizes Lula's election win in Brazil
item.description: SAO PAULO — Flavio Bolsonaro's Liberal Party on Monday recognized the outcome of Brazil's presidential runoff, despite the candidate's objections to the poll won by leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, pulled off a dramatic comeback after trailing Bolsonaro in a first-round vote, a defeat which fired up the left on the streets and social media to secure him a fourth term in office. In the end, Lula pulled around 4.4 million more votes than his rival on Sunday. Bolsonaro, a right-wing senator and 45-year-old son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, cried foul after polling was extended nationwide for two hours, at Lula's request, due to transport problems in some cities. Though Bolsonaro maintained that he will seek annulment of the presidential election, his party later distanced itself from that position and opted to accept the official vote. item.description: Golf has again become a political flashpoint in Korea after an opposition lawmaker’s allegation against first lady Kim Hea Kyung prompted an explicit denial from LPGA star Lydia Ko and a sharp rebuttal from Cheong Wa Dae. This episode drew fresh attention to why the sport remains so politically sensitive in Korea despite becoming more accessible to the public. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) claimed that Kim received an exclusive golf lesson from Ko on Oct. 20 and released a video that featured a woman who Joo claimed is the golfer. Ko, a Korean-born New Zealand LPGA Hall of Fame member, denied any involvement, saying she attended an official sponsor event that day. She warned of legal action over false information and defamatory coverage. Cheong Wa Dae also dismissed Joo’s account as false and warned that media outlets could be held responsible for repeating his assertions without verifying the facts. item.title: JYP shares surge on Japanese investment group's proposed stake purchase
item.description: JYP Entertainment shares jumped Tuesday after two little-known investors announced a potential tender offer for up to half of the K-pop company, prompting questions about their identities and ability to finance the purchase. NEXROC Group, which describes itself as a Japanese investment group, and SVCV said the previous day that they were considering buying between 25 and 50 percent of JYP’s outstanding shares. The K-pop agency behind major global acts such as Stray Kids and TWICE said it had not received any acquisition proposal from them. JYP shares opened 6.53 percent higher on the Kosdaq market and rose more than 10 percent during the session. They later gave up some of those gains to close 6.81 percent higher. The stock had already climbed in Monday’s after-hours trading on Nextrade following news of the proposed offer, finishing 14.38 percent above its regular-session close. item.title: Social media key to success for K-brands, AI expert says
item.description: Social media platforms have become a key marketplace for Korean beauty, food and fashion brands, and companies can leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to make their products go viral in global markets at minimal cost, according to an AI expert in Seoul Tuesday. Seldon Yoon, founder and CEO of Indent, a Seoul-based developer of commerce AI transformation (AX) solutions, said Reels and short-form content on Instagram and TikTok have become major channels for Korean consumers to discover and purchase new products. He added that creator content marketing has become more critical than ever, particularly for companies seeking to promote their products overseas and attract local consumers. Yoon, a former global e-commerce consultant for Samsung Electronics, cited a sharp increase in K-beauty exports since 2024 as evidence of successful overseas marketing. item.title: Kim's China trip may have been more than economic event: unification minister
item.description: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said Tuesday that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's trip to China last week may have been more than an economic event, given the makeup of his delegation. "The fact that both sides fielded their diplomatic and security teams deserves a close look," Chung said at a parliamentary audit, responding to a lawmaker's question about the meaning of Kim's surprise one-day trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday. He noted the North Korean delegation was heavy with diplomatic and security officials, and that no economic officials were present at the newly opened bridge over the Amnok River, known in China as the Yalu River. Kim was joined by his sister Kim Yo-jong, a department director of the Workers' Party of Korea; Jo Yong-won, Ri Il-hwan and Kim Song-nam, secretaries of the party's central committee; Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui; and First Vice Premier Kim Tok-hun, among others. item.title: Marine Corps commander to visit Thailand for talks on defense cooperation
item.description: The commander of Korea's Marine Corps will visit Thailand this week to discuss expanding military and defense industry ties between the two countries, Korea's armed force said Tuesday. Lt. Gen. Ju Il-suk will make a four-day trip to Bangkok and Sattahip, an eastern coastal district home to Thailand's Marine Corps base, from Tuesday through Friday, the Marine Corps said in a media note. During the visit, Ju plans to hold bilateral talks with Rear Adm. Weerachai Leeka, commander of the Royal Thai Marine Corps, and other senior military officials to discuss efforts to strengthen military cooperation and expand defense industry partnership between the two armed forces. Ju will also pay tribute at a Korean War memorial in Chonburi, honoring Thai soldiers who fell while fighting alongside Korean forces during the 1950-53 conflict. The monument is located inside the headquarters of Thailand's 21st Infantry Regiment, a core unit deployed during the war and which now symbolizes the enduring friendship between the two nations, the Marine Corps said.

item.title: Woman sentenced to 10-month prison term for spitting at police officer at election rally
item.description: A court on Tuesday sentenced a woman to 10 months in prison for spitting at a police officer and assaulting others during rallies to protest ballot shortages in June's local elections. The 45-year-old, surnamed Kim, was accused of assaulting a total of five people, including the police officer who was trying to restrain her, during rallies outside the Olympic Park Handball Gymnasium in southeastern Seoul on June 22 and 23. The Seoul Eastern District Court convicted her of obstruction of official duties and sentenced her to prison, citing her history of repeated assault and other offenses since February, as well as concerns she may reoffend. It also cited favorable factors in determining the level of punishment, including the fact that Kim admitted to her crimes, showed remorse and was diagnosed with bipolar disorder in 2024.

item.title: Korea should not sacrifice AI boom over chip dependence fears: IDB economist
item.description: Korea should capitalize on the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom rather than curb growth over concerns about its heavy reliance on chips, while building economic resilience through stabilization funds and greater structural flexibility, according to the chief economist of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), Tuesday. "I wouldn't kill the goose that lays the golden egg. It's weird to kill AI just because it's volatile. Let's find ways to adjust," Laura Alfaro, chief economist and economic counselor of the IDB, said during a press conference. "Right now, the game is AI, and Korea is growing faster than other countries. It happened because for many years you have built the production and infrastructure." Alfaro drew parallels between Korea's dependence on semiconductors and the "resource curse" in Latin America, where economies heavily reliant on natural resources are vulnerable to fluctuations in commodity prices. item.title: KT unveils AI platform Token Factory, eyes new growth business
item.description: KT is launching an artificial intelligence (AI) platform that automatically selects models for different tasks and bills customers based on token usage, as it seeks to build a new growth business by helping companies control AI costs. The telecom company announced Tuesday that it will roll out KT Token Factory on Friday, offering access to 73 AI models through a single platform, including models hosted on KT's domestic infrastructure and models from major global providers. It plans to expand the lineup to more than 500 models in November through a partnership with OpenRouter, a global AI model marketplace. The platform brings AI model selection, usage management and billing into one service, allowing businesses to access multiple models through a single API rather than signing up for and connecting to each model separately. “Competition is expanding beyond developing better AI models to finding ways to use AI effectively,” Park Sang-won, executive vice president of KT’s AX Business Division, said during a press conference at the company’s headquarters in Seoul. “The key challeng

item.title: LG Innotek Q3 net down 25.8% on fluctuating exchange rate
item.description: LG Innotek, an electronic components manufacturer under LG Group, said Tuesday its third-quarter net profit fell 25.8 percent from a year earlier, as exchange-rate fluctuations weighed on profitability. Net profit for the July-September period came to 95.2 billion won ($71.9 million), down 128.4 billion won from a year earlier, the company said in a regulatory filing. LG Innotek said its net profit declined as the Korean won weakened against the U.S. dollar when it purchased raw materials in the first half of the year but strengthened sharply by the time the company began mass-producing and shipping products in the third quarter. Operating profit for the cited period fell 53.4 percent on-year to 94.8 billion won. Sales, on the other hand, rose 18.6 percent to 6.36 trillion won, surpassing 6 trillion won for the first time in the third quarter and reaching a record high for the period. Revenue increased across all business segments from a year earlier. item.title: Special panel seeks to question ex-President Yoon over 2022 crowd crush
item.description: A special commission investigating the deadly 2022 Itaewon crowd crush plans to question former President Yoon Suk Yeol over the government's handling of the disaster, officials said Tuesday. The National Commission for the Investigation of the October 29 Itaewon Disaster outlined its plan to question the jailed ex-president and former Interior Minister Lee Sang-min in December as it shared the interim results of its probe. The commission is tasked with uncovering the cause of the tragedy, which happened during Halloween festivities in Seoul's nightlife district of Itaewon on Oct. 29, 2022, when crowds surged into a narrow alley, leaving 159 people dead and 196 injured. The panel found various shortcomings in the government response to the disaster. According to the interim probe results, the interior ministry's situation room became aware of the crowd crush at 10:48 p.m. on the night of the tragedy, but only notified then Minister Lee 43 minutes later. Yoon, who served as president at the time, made rescue instructions at 11:21 p.m., but the ministry did not deliver them for 55 minutes. T

item.title: Samsung Electronics chief to visit robotics R&D center on 4th anniversary of inauguration
item.description: Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong is set to visit the company's robotics business hub Tuesday, industry sources said, as the tech giant steps up efforts to develop robotics as a key growth engine for the future. Lee is scheduled to visit the company's research and development (R&D) center in central Seoul, in a move seen as underscoring his commitment to new businesses through on-site management, they said. Tuesday marks the fourth anniversary of Lee's inauguration as chairman in 2022. His visit to a key robotics facility, a business he has identified as a major future growth driver for Samsung, is seen as signaling the company's commitment to expand into new sectors. Lee is expected to review preparations for robotics technologies to be unveiled at CES 2027, the world's largest consumer electronics and IT trade show, in Las Vegas in January. Samsung previously outlined a strategy to gradually expand its robotics business, starting with industrial robots for manufacturing facilities, and later extending into household and service robots.

item.title: Lee, Lula swap warm words after Brazil election
item.description: Two former child factory workers who rose to become presidents exchanged warm messages following Brazil’s presidential election. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva thanked President Lee Jae Myung on Monday (local time) for congratulating him on his election victory, saying the two leaders share goals ranging from workers’ rights to environmental protection. “My dear friend President Lee Jae Myung, I sincerely thank you for your message,” Lula wrote in Portuguese on X, formerly Twitter, in response to Lee’s post a day earlier. “We will continue defending dialogue between nations, social justice, workers’ rights and environmental protection,” he wrote. “The future we want to build must offer dignity and opportunities to everyone.” He added, “I know these are goals we share. I hope we meet again soon.” Lee congratulated Lula on Monday after the Brazilian leader won a runoff election Sunday, securing an unprecedented fourth presidential term. “My dear friend and comrade President Lula, I couldn’t be happier to congratulate you on your election victory,”

item.description: Shinhan Card, KB Kookmin Card and other Korean financial firms remain hesitant to adopt Apple Pay, delaying the service’s expansion and fueling frustration among iPhone users. Hyundai Card remains the only card issuer offering Apple Pay in Korea, and it is unclear when other providers will join, according to industry officials Tuesday. Card issuers are concerned that fees paid to Apple and the cost of building payment infrastructure could undermine profitability. Questions about the fairness of fees charged for Apple Pay while Samsung Wallet, formerly Samsung Pay, remains free have added to their concerns. item.title: Everland's baby panda Shu Bao to make public debut this week
item.description: Shu Bao, the youngest member of Everland's giant panda family, will venture outside her indoor enclosure for the first time on Friday, at the age of five months. Everland, operated by Samsung C&T Resort Group, announced Monday that Shu Bao, born on June 3, will begin making regular outings at Panda World starting Thursday. A female giant panda born naturally to parents Ai Bao and Le Bao, Shu Bao is the fourth giant panda cub born in Korea, following her older sisters Fu Bao and twin pandas Rui Bao and Hui Bao. Weighing just 171 grams at birth, Shu Bao now weighs more than 9 kilograms and is growing steadily under the care of her mother Ai Bao, zookeepers and veterinarians. She began taking her first wobbly steps at around 120 days old. More recently, she has been moving around on her own near her mother and actively exploring her surroundings. Ahead of her public debut, Shu Bao has been undergoing a gradual acclimation process to help her adjust to new spaces and environments. She has been expanding her range of activities little by little, following her mother from the indoor enclosure

Controversy has arisen over comments made by USFK Commander Gen. Xavier Brunson at a seminar in Washington earlier this month, when he said that, from the U.N. Command's (UNC) perspective, Korean territory begins at the southern fence line of the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), established under the armistice that halted the 1950-53 Korean War. item.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff as AI spending accelerates
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Microsoft has offered 60,000 employees, or about 27 percent of its global workforce, voluntary buyouts as the software giant spends heavily on artificial intelligence. The company's voluntary exit offer was available to eligible employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, the company's Chief People Officer Amy Coleman wrote in a blog post Monday. “The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us,” Coleman wrote. “We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.” The company, which releases its quarterly financial results Wednesday, had approximately 223,000 full-time employees at the end of June. Shares of Microsoft Corp., based in Redmond, Washington, hit an all-time high this month. The stock rose about 1 percent on Monday. item.title: 120,000 people flock to Jamsu Bridge for 'Chicken Day' event
item.description: Hours before closing its lanes to car traffic forever, Seoul’s Jamsu Bridge hosted a record-breaking send-off powered by fried chicken. About 120,000 fried chicken enthusiasts descended on the landmark Han River span for Jamsu Bridge Chicken Day, turning the iconic structure into an open-air banquet. The poultry party served as the grand finale to this year’s car-free bridge festival, taking place just hours before the span permanently closed to vehicle traffic on Monday to begin its transformation into the river’s first pedestrian-only crossing. The festival tapped straight into a sacred local tradition: the classic riverside picnic powered by delivery fried chicken and cold drinks. Forty-six participating franchise brands, neighborhood joints and mom-and-pop vendors introduced their signature crispy creations, generating a combined 108 million won ($81,500) in sales — more than double the average food truck revenue from the festival’s spring edition, according to the Seoul Metropolitan Government. item.title: Busan webtoon festival marks 10th anniversary with 800 works by global artists
item.description: Busan will welcome about 190 webtoon artists from Korea and abroad this week for a three-day festival showcasing more than 800 works as the city marks the 10th anniversary of its international comics event. The 10th Busan Global Webtoon Festival, organized by Busan Metropolitan City with the Busan IT Industry Promotion Agency and the Busan-Gyeongnam Cartoonists Association, runs from Friday through Nov. 1 at Museum One and the Busan Cultural Contents Complex. Under the theme “Ten Years, One Story,” the festival will look back on a decade of webtoon creation while bringing artists, publishers and readers together through exhibitions, live drawing sessions and business events. Exhibitions will feature posters from previous festivals, commemorative illustrations and works by invited international artists, alongside award-winning comics and projects supported by the festival. Visitors can also attend drawing talk shows, where artists will discuss their creative processes and demonstrate how webtoons are made. item.title: Seoul offers up to 15% savings via local gift card promotion
item.description: Seoul residents can get more money back on everyday purchases starting Thursday, as the city rolls out additional cashback on local gift certificates during a nationwide shopping festival aimed at boosting consumer spending and small businesses. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that purchases made with metropolitan and district-issued Seoul Love Gift Certificates from Oct. 29 through Nov. 15 will qualify for an additional 5 percent cashback, paid in gift certificates. Combined with a 5 percent discount when buying eligible certificates and existing cashback offers, the promotion can deliver savings equivalent to as much as 15 percent of the purchase amount. For example, a shopper who buys 100,000 won worth of gift certificates at a 5 percent discount pays 95,000 won and can receive another 10,000 won in cashback if both the existing and additional 5 percent offers apply to a 100,000 won purchase. item.title: Seoul garden festival draws record 14 million visitors in 6-month run
item.description: Seoul’s biggest garden festival has drawn 14 million visitors over six months, setting a record for attendance and giving a boost to nearby businesses as the city seeks to make green spaces a larger part of urban life. The 2026 Seoul International Garden Show concluded Tuesday after running for 180 days, the longest edition yet, with attendance up 34.1 percent from 10.44 million visitors last year, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said. The festival, held from May 1 through Tuesday under the theme “Seoul, Green Culture,” expanded beyond Seoul Forest into nearby Seongsu-dong, the Konkuk University area and the Han River waterfront, with an autumn garden festival also held at Maeheon Citizens’ Forest. Organizers created 225 gardens and offered 170 programs involving guided tours, exhibitions, hands-on activities and academic events, drawing about 210,000 participants to the programs. In a city survey of 2,358 respondents conducted from Oct. 19-25, about 91 percent said they were satisfied with the event, while 82.8 percent said they intended to attend next year. item.title: AI scans Korea's highways to keep wildlife, drivers safe
item.description: On winding roads where mountainous terrain meets heavy traffic, a rustle in the brush at dusk can turn into a deadly collision within seconds. Roadkill incidents pose a constant hazard to wildlife and motorists across Korea, often resulting in severe property damage, human injuries and secondary pileups on high-speed thoroughfares. In a bid to prevent such incidents, the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment on Wednesday will launch a pilot artificial intelligence (AI)-powered roadkill prevention system along National Route 17 in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province in central Korea. Conventional mitigation measures like eco-corridors, wildlife overpasses and fencing have reduced animal fatalities along long stretches of highway. However, intersections and entrance or exit ramps remain notoriously difficult to secure without blocking traffic or human access, leaving vulnerable gaps in eco-fencing networks. item.description: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul's recent remarks on U.S. trust were intended to counter a lawmaker's doubts over Seoul's push to retake wartime operational control (OPCON) from Washington, not to question the ally's credibility, the defense ministry said Tuesday. Kang drew media attention Monday when he pushed back against an opposition lawmaker skeptical of Seoul's push for the OPCON transition, citing an uncertain global security landscape, where even a military superpower, like the United States, faces challenges in the ongoing conflict with Iran. "Because that is not the case, the OPCON transition must take place on a foundation of guaranteed trust," Kang said, advocating the OPCON road map to build a combined forces system, led by a South Korean general, with the U.S. military serving in a supporting role. item.title: Ruling party lawmaker expresses deep regret over US visa delay
item.description: Rep. Jung Chung-rae of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea criticized U.S. authorities Tuesday over a visa delay that prevented him from visiting Washington for a parliamentary audit of Seoul's diplomatic missions. Jung had initially planned to join the audit team of the parliamentary foreign affairs committee on its U.S. trip earlier this month, but was forced to switch to the Europe audit team as his visa application remained under review ahead of his planned departure. "I find the U.S. authorities' handling of the matter deeply regrettable," he said during a parliamentary audit, stressing that he had worked hard to promote friendly relations between Seoul and Washington. Jung said he had no choice but to switch to the Europe audit team out of concern that he might not be able to participate in the parliamentary audit at all. He also expressed regret that the main opposition party had turned the visa issue into a controversy about growing strains in the South Korea-U.S. alliance. item.title: Hanwha Ocean's Q3 net falls 46% despite strong operating earnings
item.description: Korean shipbuilder Hanwha Ocean said Tuesday its third-quarter net profit dropped 46.1 percent from a year earlier, despite strong operating earnings driven by increased sales of high value-added vessels and naval ships. Net profit stood at 145.1 billion won ($109.6 million) in the July-September period, down from 269.4 billion won a year earlier, the company said in a regulatory filing. Operating profit jumped 67.6 percent on-year to 485.7 billion won, while sales rose 12.9 percent to 3.41 trillion won over the period. Revenue from commercial ships reached 2.7 trillion won, while sales from the naval and specialized vessel segment totaled 363 billion won. Hanwha Ocean attributed the rise in operating profit to increased deliveries of high value-added commercial vessels and stronger revenue from its naval shipbuilding business, including submarines and surface vessels. item.title: Mercedes-Benz Korea marks 20 years of technician training
item.description: Mercedes-Benz Korea is marking the 20th anniversary of its automotive technician training program by strengthening a talent development pipeline that connects early career exploration with specialized training and employment, the carmaker said Tuesday. The automaker has built a series of education programs through the Mercedes-Benz Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Committee, starting with the Mobile Academy industry-academia partnership program and extending to the Automotive Electric Traineeship (AET) and subsequent technical training for technicians working in its authorized service network. Launched in 2014, Mobile Academy helps high school and university students explore career opportunities in the automotive industry through lectures, technical education and mentoring from industry professionals. Its university program also introduces students to job openings at authorized dealerships, giving them opportunities to understand workplace requirements and explore potential career paths. item.description: The University of Seoul will hold its 2026 Major Information Session on Thursday at its Centennial Memorial Hall to expand students’ options for choosing their majors. The university said the session, organized as part of the government’s University Innovation Support Project, aims to help students interested in pursuing multiple majors and those enrolled in the School of Liberal Studies design their own academic paths. A total of 31 schools, departments, project groups and administrative offices, including the Office of Academic Affairs, will participate in the session. At each booth, representatives will introduce major-specific curricula and flexible academic options, including double majors, minors, changes of major and modular curricula. They will also provide road maps outlining degree requirements for each major, along with personalized consultations to help students plan their academic paths. item.title: Nuclear watchdog approves 10-year lifespan extension for Kori units 3, 4
item.description: The country's nuclear watchdog decided Tuesday to extend the operational life of two nuclear reactors located on the country's southeastern coast by an additional 10 years. The approval by the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission (NSSC) came four years after the Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP), the state-run power operator, requested the agency review the restart of Kori units 3 and 4. The two pressurized water reactors of 1,025 megawatts gross capacity had stopped power generation after 40 years of commercial use that began in 1985 and 1986, respectively. The country's nuclear watchdog had approved last year a 10-year extension for the Kori-2 light-water reactor. The decision also came after the commission approved early this month the accident management program for the two nuclear reactors — a document that outlines preparations, including strategies to maintain safe conditions, to prevent accidents and mitigate any fallout if a nuclear accident occurs. Accordingly, Kori-3 will be able to operate till September 2034 and Kori-4 will run until August 2035.

item.title: Shinhan Financial Group Q3 net profit up 10.9% on rising interest income
item.description: Shinhan Financial Group said Tuesday its net income rose more than 10 percent in the third quarter from a year earlier driven by a rise in interest income. The banking group posted a net profit of 1.6 trillion won ($1.2 billion) for the July-September period, up 10.9 percent from a year earlier. Operating profit for the three-month period stood at 1.9 trillion won, down 2.4 percent from a year ago, while revenue rose 95.9 percent to 18.64 trillion won. The earnings met market expectations. The average estimate of net profit by analysts stood at 1.61 trillion won, according to a survey by Yonhap Infomax, the financial data firm of Yonhap News Agency. Shinhan then said its interest income increased 8.3 percent on-year to 3.2 trillion won in the third quarter but its commission income declined 18.1 percent to 790.2 billion won. In the first nine months of the year, Shinhan Financial racked up 5.03 trillion won in net profit, up 12.7 percent from a year earlier, outnumbering the group's annual net profit of 4.97 trillion won for 2025. item.title: How Trump's 'little detour' to Iran became a roadblock in the midterm elections
item.description: WASHINGTON — Noor Dubow says he regularly votes for Republican candidates who he believes align with his economic views — even though he's never been a fan of Donald Trump , finding himself repelled by some of the president's dehumanizing rhetoric toward immigrants. But this year, when Dubow cast his early ballot in the midterm election , he found himself tipping more toward Democrats because of his frustration with Trump's decision to go to war with Iran. “Where are the Republicans in Congress?” asked Dubow, 44, a dispatcher at a trucking logistics firm in Columbus, Ohio, where he has a bird's eye view of the disruption that surging fuel prices are having on the economy. "Why aren't the Republicans holding Trump accountable?” The Iran war, which Trump often describes as a “little detour,” has emerged as an unforced liability for the president, who once promised to keep the U.S. out of foreign wars. item.title: Defense chief heads to Philippines for ASEAN-led defense ministers' meeting
item.description: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul heads to the Philippines Tuesday to attend a regional defense ministers’ meeting, his first multilateral security gathering since taking office, the Ministry of National Defense said. Kang will take part in the 13th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) on Thursday, the ministry said. The ADMM-Plus brings together defense ministers from the 11 ASEAN member states and eight of the bloc’s dialogue partners, including Korea, the United States and Japan. Launched in 2010, it serves as a platform for defense cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region. The Philippines, which holds the rotating ASEAN chair this year, is hosting the meeting in Lapu-Lapu City in the province of Cebu. At this year’s meeting, participants will assess the regional security environment and discuss ways to strengthen defense cooperation for peace and stability. item.title: Korea consolidates traditional arts agencies to amplify cultural reach
item.description: The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Tuesday it will merge the Gugak Broadcasting Foundation and the Korean Traditional Performing Arts Foundation to build a stronger base for promoting "gugak," or traditional Korean music, and other traditional arts. The move is part of a government plan announced Sept. 3 to reform the functions of public institutions, under which bodies with overlapping roles are to be merged or reorganized. The Gugak Broadcasting Foundation, which operates the radio station Gugak FM, has worked to distribute gugak content and make the genre more accessible to the public through broadcasting. The Korean Traditional Performing Arts Foundation, established in 2007, has supported the creation and production of traditional performing arts and trained professionals in the field, while working to expand opportunities for the public to enjoy such performances. By combining the two organizations, the ministry aims to make its policies more efficient and provide comprehensive support for the promotion and spread of gugak and traditional arts. item.title: Seoul, Tokyo form united front against counterfeiters, drug traffickers
item.description: As K-pop, Korean cosmetics and fashion continue to capture global consumers, a darker shadow industry has grown alongside them: counterfeiters pumping out fake Korean goods, and international smuggling syndicates attempting to move illicit narcotics across borders. In response, Korea’s top customs official is launching a broad diplomatic campaign to enlist global enforcement agencies in cracking down on intellectual property theft and drug trafficking. Lee Jong-wook, head of the Korea Customs Service (KCS), will initiate the campaign on Oct. 29, during a high-level summit with his Japanese counterpart. The bilateral meeting marks the starting line of an ambitious diplomatic expansion aimed at building real-time information-sharing networks with key trading partners across Asia, Europe and the Americas. During the upcoming Tokyo summit, KCS said Lee plans to formally request that Japanese customs authorities streamline application processing for Korean companies seeking border enforcement of their intellectual property rights. item.title: Korea prepares real life space sweeper to hunt orbiting junk
item.description: Science fiction is quietly becoming an engineering reality in Korea. Long a staple of science fiction and brought to life in the 2021 Korean blockbuster film "Space Sweepers," the concept of orbital sanitation vessels is becoming a reality as Korea’s space agency prepares a mission to clean up the increasingly crowded skies. The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) announced a milestone step, Tuesday, in its effort to tackle orbital debris. Meeting at Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology's (KAIST) Satellite Technology Research Center in Daejeon, officials completed the System Integration Readiness Review for the Active Debris Removal Satellite (ADR-SAT). Having cleared technical evaluations from an independent panel of experts, engineers will begin final assembly of the flight model next month, setting the stage for a launch aboard Korea's homegrown Nuri rocket in 2027. The initiative comes at a critical juncture for low Earth orbit. Cho made the remarks during a parliamentary audit of the foreign and unification ministries, responding to Rep. item.title: International Ministerial Conference on Nuclear Power kicks off in Korea
item.description: A quadrennial, high-level policy event organized by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) kicked off its three-day run in the western port city of Incheon on Tuesday, facilitating discussion on the progress of new nuclear technologies, effective regulation and opportunities for industry growth. The International Ministerial Conference on Nuclear Power was held for the first time in Korea this year, bringing together some 800 participants, including government officials from 60 member nations, non-governmental organizations and companies in the nuclear industry. The event comes as global investments in the nuclear sector grows, amid the rapid rise in artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced industries fueling demand for energy, Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said in an opening address. "Nuclear power is a key source (of energy) that can provide a large amount of low-carbon electricity day and night," he said, noting that global nuclear capacity could more than triple from last year's level by 2060. item.title: N. Korean artillery deployed along western border not seen as new weapon system: JCS
item.description: North Korean artillery deployed along the western front line appears to be legacy weaponry rather than a new system that Pyongyang recently threatened to forward-deploy, a South Korean military official said Tuesday. What appears to be North Korean self-propelled artillery has been spotted farther south than its usual positions along the western front near the inter-Korean border, close enough to be captured by South Korean media cameras. Photos taken by Yonhap News Agency from an observation deck at a park in Gimpo, west of Seoul, showed what experts say appears to be a 122 millimeter self-propelled howitzer deployed in a coastal border area of Kaepung County, Hwanghae Province. "Our understanding is that North Korea has deployed legacy artillery along coastal areas in plain view," the South's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) spokesperson Capt. Jang Do-young said in a press briefing when asked for comment on the development. item.title: FTC to slap $15.1 mil. fine on Samsung Electronics for misleading gaming ads
item.description: Korea's antitrust watchdog said Tuesday it has decided to impose a tentative fine of 20 billion won ($15.1 million) on Samsung Electronics for misleading advertisements concealing features limiting the performance of its Galaxy S21 and S22 smartphones during gaming. The Fair Trade Commission's (FTC) decision concerns the two smartphone series, released in 2021 and 2022, respectively, along with the Galaxy Tab S8 tablet series launched in 2022. According to the FTC, the Korean tech giant failed to disclose that its game optimizing service (GOS) imposed preset performance limits as soon as certain demanding gaming apps were launched, while promoting the products' advanced gaming capabilities in advertisements. GOS is a heat management system for gaming apps. Under its game-specific policies, it capped maximum CPU and GPU performance regardless of the device's temperature or other conditions. The limitations could cause freezes, lag and reduced graphics quality during gameplay, the FTC said. item.title: [INTERVIEW] Korea's tungsten mine could help US cut reliance on China, Tungco CEO says
item.description: As the United States seeks to reduce its reliance on China for tungsten, a critical mineral used in semiconductors and defense systems, producers in allied nations such as Korea could help fill the supply gap, according to a Kentucky-based tungsten recycling executive. Cliff Nance, owner and CEO of Tungco, said “more production from trusted allies” could help the United States reduce its reliance on China, which dominates the global tungsten supply chain. He welcomed the prospect of the U.S. importing tungsten from the Sangdong mine in Yeongwol, Gangwon Province, where Almonty Korea Tungsten Corp. (AKTC) completed production facilities in September. “Almonty’s Sangdong mine is a positive development for both Korea and the U.S.,” Nance said in an interview with The Korea Times. "Breaking China’s dominance of tungsten requires more production from trusted allies, and Korea can play an important role." item.title: Netanyahu's political survival on line as Israel votes
item.description: JERUSALEM — Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a fight for political survival in Israel's election on Tuesday, with voters weighing his leadership after the 2023 Hamas-led attacks, wars in Gaza and with Iran, and Israel's deepening international isolation. Yet Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader with 19 years in office, remains a formidable survivor, with nationalist politics increasingly entrenched and Israel's fragmented system potentially leaving him best placed to form a government. Opinion polls show a close race between Netanyahu's Likud party and its right-wing allies and a rival alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff and security hawk with backers on the right and in the centre. Netanyahu is campaigning on his wartime leadership and his alliance with U.S. President Donald Trump, who has endorsed him and joined Israel in waging war on Iran. Netanyahu said on Sunday that Trump was prepared to act again to “finally” remove the Iranian threat, but only if Netanyahu remained in power. item.title: Hyundai Motor's slide accelerates in Europe, China
item.description: Hyundai Motor Group is losing ground in key overseas markets amid declining sales in Europe and a renewed slump in China, raising concerns about its global strategy beyond the United States. Hyundai Motor and Kia sold around 770,000 vehicles in Europe from January to September, down 3.4 percent from a year earlier, according to data from the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association. The decline contrasted with a 6.3 percent rise in the overall European market, dragging the group’s combined market share down 0.7 percentage point to 7.3 percent during the same period. The weakness largely stemmed from Hyundai Motor, which saw European sales fell 13.2 percent to around 349,000 vehicles. Kia’s sales rose 6.6 percent to around 421,900, allowing the affiliate to overtake Hyundai as the group’s bigger seller in the region. The latest data indicates growing pressure on Hyundai Motor Group, as established European brands and Chinese manufacturers compete more aggressively on electric vehicles (EVs), pricing and model selection. item.title: Investigation body chief attends Cabinet meeting for 2nd time amid controversy
item.description: Kim Ji-yong, the inaugural chief of the Serious Crime Investigation Agency (SCIA), once again attended a Cabinet meeting presided over by President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday, despite opposition criticism that his presence could undermine the agency's neutrality and independence. Kim's attendance marked the second time he had joined the weekly Cabinet meeting since heading the SCIA, which was launched Oct. 2 as part of a criminal justice overhaul stripping prosecutors of their independent investigative powers. Kim Jong-chul, acting commissioner general of the Korean National Police Agency, and acting Prosecutor General Lee Jeong-hyun also showed up at the Cabinet meeting. During a recent parliamentary audit of the Lee administration, a heated debate erupted over whether it is appropriate for heads of investigative and prosecutorial agencies to attend Cabinet meetings. item.title: Supreme Court finalizes 3-yr prison term for ex-commander over Marine's death
item.description: The Supreme Court on Tuesday finalized a three-year prison term for a former Marine commander for negligently causing the death of a young Marine in 2023. Lim Seong-geun, former commander of the Marine Corps 1st Division, was convicted of causing death or injury through occupational negligence and violating orders under the Military Criminal Act, in connection with the death of Cpl. Chae Su-geun and the injury of other Marines during search operations for heavy rain victims in Yecheon, some 160 kilometers southeast of Seoul, in July 2023. The top court upheld a lower court's three-year sentence for Lim, ruling there were no errors in the interpretation of the law. Lim was indicted by special counsel Lee Myeong-hyeon's team in November 2025 for allegedly sending the Marines on the search mission without providing life vests and other safety equipment. He was also indicted for allegedly disobeying orders to transfer operational control to the Army during the search.

item.title: President Lee says Korea should learn from European protests to sustain growth
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung said Tuesday that Korea should learn from growing public protests in Europe, citing low growth as a potential reason for the unrest and stressing the importance of ensuring sustained growth at home. The president made the remarks at a Cabinet meeting, as a wave of protests and mass demonstrations over rising living costs and economic inequality has swept across European nations, including France, Spain and Italy. "As large-scale protests have occurred recently in many European countries, social confusion and conflict have ensued," Lee said. "We should take the European situation as an example of what not to do." Lee said many experts pointed to high energy and living costs, a stagnant economy and accumulated inequality as factors gripping Europe, adding, "The biggest and most fundamental reason might be low growth." "Prolonged low growth has worsened youth unemployment and (economic) polarization and weakened fiscal status, shaking social stability from the root," the president said of the European situation. item.title: IVE teams up with Krafton for PUBG: Battlegrounds collaboration
item.description: K-pop girl group IVE will appear in Krafton’s hit battle royale game PUBG: Battlegrounds next month, the Korean game company said Tuesday. The collaboration centers on “Love Dive,” one of IVE’s signature songs, and will include video content and in-game items. Battle royale is a genre of online shooting games in which a large number of players compete until only one player or team survives. Krafton first hinted at the partnership with a teaser image last week. The company released the collaboration’s key art Tuesday and planned to unveil a teaser trailer at 6 p.m. the same day, showing a themed area on Rondo, one of the game’s maps, and some of the new items. A main trailer starring the IVE members will follow on Nov. 1. In it, the members recreate the concept and outfits from their “Love Dive” promotions. The video will also debut a new arrangement that blends the original song with music from the game. The themed area, inspired by the song’s music video, will recreate key scenes and the video’s mood to fit the game environment. Krafton will also release character skin

item.title: Korean job postings grow longer, more detailed in AI era: JobKorea
item.description: Job postings in Korea have become longer and more detailed over the past five years as companies spell out the specific skills they want amid the spread of artificial intelligence (AI), according to an analysis released Tuesday by job portal JobKorea. The online recruitment platform, operated by Worxphere, analyzed the text of job postings published on its site from 2021 through the third quarter of this year. The share of postings that included a separate section on preferred qualifications nearly doubled from 14.5 percent in 2021 to 28.3 percent this year. Postings listing required qualifications rose from 18.6 percent to 27.3 percent over the same period. Since 2025, preferred qualifications have appeared more often than required ones. Postings also grew longer. The median length rose 79 percent from 483 Korean characters, including spaces, in 2021 to 864 characters this year, while the average increased 32 percent from 817 to 1,077 characters. The share of postings that included a separate section on preferred qualifications nearly doubled from 14.5 percent in 2021 to 28.3 percent this year. Postings listing required qualifications rose from 18.6 percent to 27.3 percent over the same period. Since 2025, preferred qualifications have appeared more often than required ones. Postings also grew longer. The median length rose 79 percent from 483 Korean characters, including spaces, in 2021 to 864 characters this year, while the average increased 32 percent from 817 to 1,077 characters. item.title: Taihan wins turnkey 380-kV power grid deal in Germany
item.description: Taihan Cable & Solution won a turnkey contract to build an extra-high-voltage power grid in Germany, expanding its presence in the European market, the Korean cable maker said Tuesday. The project was secured by the company’s Dutch subsidiary, Taihan Netherlands, through a turnkey arrangement, under which a single contractor handles a project from start to finish. The subsidiary will oversee the entire project, including local engineering and construction, while the Korean headquarters will manufacture and supply key materials such as extra-high-voltage cables and joints. Taihan said in a regulatory filing the same day that its headquarters signed a supply contract worth about 115 billion won ($87 million) with the subsidiary. The total value of the turnkey deal is higher, but the company did not disclose the figure or the client, citing a confidentiality agreement. The project involves building a 380-kilovolt (kV) underground grid, the highest voltage used in Germany’s underground alternating current power network. item.title: LG CNS wins global certification for compliance management system
item.description: LG CNS has secured international certification for its compliance management system, strengthening its efforts to meet growing regulatory demands across artificial intelligence, cloud computing and data center operations. The Korean IT services company said Tuesday it had received ISO 37301 certification, an international standard established by the International Organization for Standardization to help organizations manage obligations involving laws, regulations, internal policies and ethical requirements. LRQA, an international assurance and certification provider formerly known as Lloyd’s Register Quality Assurance, conducted the assessment, examining compliance practices across LG CNS’ major business areas, including AI, cloud services, data centers and software development and maintenance. The review included examinations of systems and documentation, interviews with executives and employees responsible for compliance and checks of actual business records. item.title: Coway air purifier earns spot on TIME's best inventions list
item.description: Coway’s latest air purifier earned a place among TIME’s best inventions of 2026, highlighting the Korean company’s efforts to make cleaner indoor air more accessible through improved filtration, quieter operation and automated monitoring. The Airmega Mighty2 (AP-1512N) was selected in TIME’s household category, with the magazine describing it as “the double-duty air purifier” for combining air purification with real-time indoor air quality monitoring. TIME evaluated nominations from its editors and correspondents worldwide, considering originality, effectiveness, ambition and impact, according to Coway’s announcement Monday. The Mighty2 uses a three-stage filtration system featuring a high-efficiency particulate air filter that is 20 percent larger than its predecessor and an activated carbon filter that is 45 percent larger, designed to capture allergens, dust, pollen, mold, cooking fumes and wildfire smoke. item.title: Hyundai Engineering targets global SMR market with US partnerships
item.description: Hyundai Engineering is stepping up its push into the global small modular reactor (SMR) market, signing agreements with two U.S. nuclear technology developers to pursue demonstration projects involving next-generation reactor designs. The Korean engineering company said Tuesday it signed memorandums of understanding with Nano Nuclear Energy, known as NNE, and ARC Clean Technology to explore cooperation on fourth-generation SMRs, as demand for reliable, low-carbon electricity grows alongside artificial intelligence and data center expansion. Under its agreement with NNE, Hyundai Engineering plans to support the KRONOS micro modular reactor project at the campus of University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, aimed to provide heat for the campus and advance carbon neutrality goals. item.title: GNI per capita 'almost certain' to reach $40,000 in 2026: finance ministry
item.description: Korea is "almost certain" to reach a gross national income (GNI) per capita of $40,000 this year, the finance ministry said Tuesday, as Asia's No. 4 economy grew 1 percent in the third quarter from the previous three-month period, driven by strong exports and investment. The Ministry of Finance and Economy made the assessment following the release of advance third-quarter data from the Bank of Korea (BOK), which would mark a new milestone after the country's per capita GNI, a gauge of the population's purchasing power, first surpassed the $30,000 mark in 2014. "Korea maintained solid growth despite a high base effect from the first half, raising the possibility of growth in the mid-3 percent range this year," the finance ministry said. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said this month Korea's economic growth for 2026 could range from 3.4 percent to 3.6 percent. "The GNI per capita is almost certain to hit $40,000 for the first time ever," it added. The International Monetary Fund also recently projected Korea's per capita GNI would reach the $40,000 level in 2026 and $50,000 in 2028. The fina

item.title: Hanwha Ocean steps up push into global warship market
item.description: Hanwha Ocean is bolstering its push for its warship business overseas, targeting strategic markets across Europe, Southeast Asia and Latin America as it moves to strengthen its position in the global naval defense industry. The shipbuilder is leveraging its submarine design and construction expertise, surface warship experience and large-scale production capacity to pursue new export opportunities. Hanwha Ocean is the only Korean company to have participated in all three Korean Destroyer eXperimental (KDX) programs and all multi-phase Jangbogo submarine development projects. The KDX program is an initiative by the Republic of Korea Navy to modernize its destroyer fleet. The company's overseas naval business builds on its previous export record and a growing pipeline of potential contracts. Under its former name, Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering, Hanwha Ocean accumulated overseas submarine project experience through programs in Indonesia. item.title: Special counsel searches Seoul handball arena in ballot shortage probe
item.description: A special counsel team on Tuesday searched a handball arena that served as a vote counting center earlier this year as part of a probe into an unprecedented shortage of ballots during the June 3 local elections. Special counsel Lee Tae-han sent investigators to execute a search-and-seizure warrant at the Olympic Park Handball Gymnasium in southeastern Seoul, to secure election records and surveillance camera footage. It marked the special counsel team's first search and seizure of the arena since its investigation launched last month. Lee's team said it plans to review the secured material to investigate the circumstances surrounding the ballot shortage and allegations of poor election management by the National Election Commission. Multiple polling stations reported ballot shortages during the local elections, and some voters were forced to turn back without casting their votes, sparking major public outcry. The search took place a day before the special counsel team's inspection of voter ballots stored at the gymnasium. The site houses 2.47 million ballot papers cast in Seoul's southeast

item.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro says court banned him from leaving country
item.description: RIO DE JANEIRO — Flavio Bolsonaro on Monday said a Supreme Court justice had banned him from leaving Brazil, one day after he lost the country's presidential election and refused to concede defeat. The right-wing senator received 48.2 percent of the vote compared to 51.8 percent for incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. "I was served with an order to hand over my passports and I am also banned from leaving the country," he said in a video posted to Instagram. Bolsonaro, the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro, denounced "a clear attempt to intimidate me." The senator is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering during the financing of a biopic about his father. He denies any wrongdoing. The 45-year-old said the decision to seize his passport stems from a statement made by his brother, US-based former lawmaker Eduardo Bolsonaro, that Flavio would have to leave Brazil if he lost the election. item.title: Dongwon F&B enters frozen chicken market with Kebasak
item.description: Dongwon F&B has entered the frozen chicken market with two products under its new Kebasak brand, using specialized batter technology and a double-frying process to deliver a crispy texture. The products are designed to let consumers enjoy restaurant-quality chicken at home without delivery fees or waiting times. The lineup includes Kebasak Fried Chicken, seasoned with spicy Cajun spices, and Kebasak Chili Mayo Chicken, which combines a pungent chili flavor with savory mayonnaise. Dongwon F&B uses its proprietary Air-Crisp technology, which creates tiny air bubbles in the batter to enhance crispiness and distribute fat evenly. The company said the technique helps maintain consistent quality and prevents the coating from becoming soggy quickly. The chicken is prepared through a double-frying process, with chicken thigh meat coated in batter made from an optimized ratio of flour and water before being fried at low and high temperatures. The method produces a crispy exterior and moist interior. Both products use 100 percent chicken thigh meat to deliver a tender texture and juicy flavor. High

item.description: Jisoo of K-pop powerhouse BLACKPINK is set to drop "Addicted," the second prerelease single from her upcoming debut full-length solo album, Friday, her agency said Tuesday. The track will premiere simultaneously across domestic and international music streaming platforms at 8 a.m., according to her label, Blissoo. In the fast-paced K-pop market, releasing advance singles ahead of a complete studio album has become a crucial promotional strategy to build global fan momentum. The announcement follows a multiday promotional rollout. item.title: Localized Russia-Ukraine ceasefire takes effect in Oleshky in deal brokered by Melania Trump
item.description: MYKOLAIV, Ukraine — A localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission led by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. The pause in fighting started at 3 a.m. in Ukraine to allow an aid mission into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine later this week. According to her office, Melania Trump led talks with civilian negotiators from Russia and Ukraine after meeting with United Nations officials who briefed her on the situation in the town. The aid mission is planned ahead of a new round of U.S.-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine expected next month and aimed at ending the war after more than 4½ years of fighting. Up to 2,000 people are stranded in Oleshky with dwindling supplies of food and medicine. They have been unable to leave because of explosive mines and drone attacks in the area, according to the U.N. The ceasefire is due to last through Saturday, or longer, amid deep mistrust between Russia and Ukraine that has thwarted previous attempts at ceasefires. item.title: KRX activates buy-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp rise
item.description: Korea's bourse operator on Tuesday activated a buy-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the stock index rose sharply. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes at 10:13 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). After opening 3.46 percent higher, the KOSPI gained 241.75 points, or 4.42 percent, to 5,711.22 as of 10:20 a.m. The index rallied on the back of overnight Wall Street gains, as renewed optimism over artificial intelligence (AI) and falling oil prices boosted investor sentiment. A buy-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index rises 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

item.title: HYBE expands global operations with new label services chief
item.description: K-pop powerhouse HYBE is sharpening its international operations, appointing industry veteran Juan Arenas to steer a newly streamlined global division aimed at uniting distribution, marketing and artist promotion across its worldwide label network. The company said Tuesday that Arenas, chief intellectual property officer at HYBE America, would serve as president of the label's Global Label Services, expanding an existing operation into a centralized support organization for labels across all of its global entities. The division will coordinate global distribution strategies, manage supply chains and oversee relationships with regional distributors and online and offline platforms, while tailoring marketing and promotional campaigns to local markets. HYBE launched its Label Services operation in the United States in 2024 as part of its HYBE 2.0 growth strategy, subsequently extending the model to Korea and other markets. The latest restructuring reflects HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk’s “multi-home, multi-genre” strategy, which seeks to strengthen infrastructure across major music marke
