item.title: Nexon partners with Chernin Entertainment to bring ARC Raiders, The Finals to screen
item.description: Nexon has signed a partnership with Hollywood production company Chernin Entertainment to develop film and television adaptations of its video games ARC Raiders and The Finals, the Tokyo-listed game company said Tuesday. Under the deal, Chernin Entertainment will lead the development of film and TV projects based on the two titles, both made by Embark Studios, Nexon's Stockholm-based subsidiary. Financial terms and release schedules were not disclosed. ARC Raiders is a survival action game set on a post-apocalyptic Earth ruled by machines called ARC, in which players scavenge for resources while fighting both the machines and one another. Released last October, it drew 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms within two weeks and has since sold more than 16 million copies worldwide, Nexon said. The game won best multiplayer game at The Game Awards, Online Game of the Year at the D.I.C.E. Awards and the multiplayer prize at the BAFTA Games Awards. Under the deal, Chernin Entertainment will lead the development of film and TV projects based on the two titles, both made by Embark Studios, Nexon's Stockholm-based subsidiary. Financial terms and release schedules were not disclosed. ARC Raiders is a survival action game set on a post-apocalyptic Earth ruled by machines called ARC, in which players scavenge for resources while fighting both the machines and one another. Released last October, it drew 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms within two weeks and has since sold more than 16 million copies worldwide, Nexon said. The game won best multiplayer game at The Game Awards, Online Game of the Year at the D.I.C.E. Awards and the multiplayer prize at the BAFTA Games Awards. item.description: The Asian Games and the Chuseok holiday have come and gone, and the air has finally turned crisp with the arrival of autumn, but K-pop's race to the top of the charts is running as hot as ever. October brings more than a dozen notable releases, building to a single day on Oct. 26 when three of the industry's biggest names put out new music at once. Before then, the calendar fills with quick returns from rising groups, a virtual idol act fresh off its first stadium show and a new solo EP from BLACKPINK's Lisa. item.title: LG Uplus, Woori Bank team up to spot voice phishing calls in real time
item.description: Mobile carrier LG Uplus has partnered with Woori Bank to feed real-time scam alerts to the lender, helping block fraudulent wire transfers while victims are still on the line with voice phishing scammers. Voice phishing refers to phone scams in which callers pose as prosecutors, police or bank employees to trick victims into transferring money. Under the service, ixi-O, the mobile carrier's artificial intelligence (AI)-powered call app, flags a suspicious call and sends the risk information to the bank. Woori Bank then steps up monitoring of the customer through its fraud detection system, which screens transactions for abnormal patterns. If a suspicious transaction follows, the bank will take protective steps under its internal procedures, such as additional identity verification or a notice to the customer, LG Uplus said. The company said banks' anti-phishing efforts have focused on transaction data such as account transfers, making it difficult to catch warning signs before money moves. item.title: Jeju Air ramps up China routes ahead of winter travel surge
item.description: Jeju Air will add flights on four China routes this winter and has secured rights to launch services from Incheon to Beijing and Changsha, the Korean low-cost carrier said Tuesday. The airline said it was allocated traffic rights in September for seven weekly Incheon-Beijing flights and four weekly Incheon-Changsha flights. Traffic rights are government-issued permits that set how often a carrier may fly an international route. In April, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport awarded it rights on five other routes: Busan-Guilin, Busan-Shanghai, Daegu-Shanghai, Jeju-Chengdu and Jeju-Chongqing. The allocations allow Jeju Air to serve 13 Chinese cities, the most among Korean low-cost carriers, the company said. It currently operates 14 China routes, including nonscheduled services. Changsha, the capital of Hunan province, is a gateway to Zhangjiajie, a mountain area known for its sandstone pillars. item.title: Jongmyo Shrine, Basilica of Saint-Denis exchange French, Korean visitor guides
item.description: Situated nearly 5,500 miles apart, Seoul’s Jongmyo Shrine and the Basilica Cathedral of Saint-Denis near Paris share a remarkably similar historic duty: serving as the final resting places for two nations' royal dynasties. Now, the two historic sites are swapping native languages to welcome an expanding influx of international travelers. Officials from Korea’s Royal Palaces and Tombs Center met with France’s Centre des Monuments Nationaux inside the Saint-Denis cathedral last week to officially exchange freshly published visitor guidebooks — offering French text for Jongmyo and Korean for Saint-Denis. The initiative marks the first concrete deliverable under a cultural collaboration agreement signed during a bilateral summit in April. Both institutions sought to deepen diplomatic and heritage ties by linking their premier royal burial sites. Jongmyo Shrine, built in 1395, houses the spirit tablets of Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) kings and queens. item.title: SKT showcases AI battlefield command tools at Army festival
item.description: SK Telecom, Korea’s largest wireless telecommunications operator, was the lone private-sector company at Korea’s Ground Forces Festival, where it spent five days showcasing artificial intelligence (AI) and communications technologies designed to reshape how military commanders gather information, make decisions and stay connected in contested environments. SKT said Tuesday that it participated in the festival from Thursday to Monday at Gyeryongdae airfield in Gyeryong, South Chungcheong Province, presenting AI defense transformation technologies under its T military brand. The centerpiece was its AI staff system, which combines a data platform, ontology technology and digital twins to connect battlefield information and help commanders assess situations and make tactical decisions. The system is designed to bring together data generated by troops and equipment, as well as drones, robots and sensors, then deliver relevant information quickly enough to support faster decisions. Visitors and military officials could follow the process from data collection and analysis to digital battlef

item.title: 28 IP addresses behind recent hacking attacks against Korean financial institutions: watchdog
item.description: The country's financial watchdog has pinpointed 28 internet protocol (IP) addresses in the United States, Japan and 10 other countries used for a series of recent hacking attacks Korean financial institutions, industry sources said Tuesday. Several financial companies, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank, suffered back-to-back leaks of customer information in recent hacking attacks last week, raising concerns that more firms might have suffered data breaches. According to the sources, the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) has shortlisted IP addresses in 12 countries as of 6:00 p.m. on Monday, which are presumed to have been used for the artificial intelligence (AI) agent-backed hacking. But it has not been able to pinpoint the locations of some of the IP addresses, they said. Local financial firms have been in a hurry to check their own security systems to fend off any additional hacking attempts. item.title: LG CNS unveils blockchain tech to help banks issue stablecoins, tokens
item.description: LG CNS launched a blockchain infrastructure platform designed to help financial institutions build services around stablecoins, tokenized securities and real-world assets as Korea’s financial sector moves toward broader use of digital assets. The information technology services giant said Tuesday that its new platform, called KITL, provides four core functions: digital wallets, transaction processing, fee payment and transaction data collection. KITL is designed to address infrastructure needs that arise when financial institutions handle assets on public blockchains, where transactions occur outside systems directly controlled by banks, securities firms and other service providers. Its wallet system can generate private keys only when signatures are required and discard them afterward, allowing institutions to issue wallets at large scale without continuously expanding hardware security module capacity, the company said. item.title: 2026 Genesis GV80 Hybrid pairs twin-turbo V6 with EV-style torque
item.description: Genesis has entered Korea’s rear-wheel-drive hybrid luxury SUV market with the launch of the GV80 Hybrid, pairing a 2.5-liter turbo engine with an electric motor system designed to deliver stronger performance, improved fuel economy and a quieter ride. Genesis, Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand, began selling the GV80 Hybrid on Tuesday, marking its first model to use a rear-wheel-drive-based 2.5 turbo hybrid system. The SUV produces a combined 352 horsepower, about 16 percent more than the 304 horsepower offered by the 2.5 turbo gasoline model, while achieving combined fuel economy of 12 kilometers per liter in the 19-inch, two-wheel-drive, five-seat configuration. GV80 Hybrid uses a parallel hybrid system combining a P1 starter motor and a P2 drive motor capable of producing up to 59.1 kilowatts, with the latter handling propulsion and regenerative braking. item.title: Lee orders dedication of personnel, resources to handling hacking attacks
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung instructed the government Tuesday to dedicate personnel and resources to minimizing damage from a recent series of hacking attacks at financial firms. Lee gave the order at a Cabinet meeting in response to revelations that the attacks exposed customer information at seven companies, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank. "In some hacking cases, details have emerged of the possible use of artificial intelligence (AI), causing the people to feel great concern and anxiety," he said. "Please carry out a swift and clear determination of the circumstances and concentrate personnel and resources on minimizing damage." Police said the same day that an investigation has been launched into the cyber attacks, with a 28-member team looking into charges of violations of the information and communications network law. Lee called for high vigilance not only within the government and business sectors but across society, saying AI-driven hacking methods are increasing the scope of damage to previously unseen levels. item.title: Unification ministry vows dialogue over hard-line response to DMZ blast
item.description: The unification ministry said Tuesday it will keep seeking peaceful solutions to inter-Korean issues, reiterating its commitment to seeking dialogue following the recent explosions of North Korea-planted land mines inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that injured three South Korean military officers. The statement came a day after Seoul's defense ministry concluded North Korea was behind the Sept. 21 land mine explosions. The ministry said it would consider the next steps with relevant government agencies, including the defense ministry. "We will keep working to break the vicious cycle of hostility and confrontation, and to build a virtuous cycle of peace and prosperity," it said, adding it would pursue lasting peace "through communication rather than a hard-line standoff." The South Korean military on Monday announced the final results of its joint investigation with the U.N. Command into the blast, confirming its preliminary findings that resin antipersonnel mines deliberately planted by Pyongyang south of the Military Demarcation Line caused the explosion. item.title: S. Korea, US aligned on N. Korea policy, denuclearization of Korean Peninsula: FM Cho
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Korea and the United States are aligned in their North Korea policy and remain committed to the goal of denuclearizing the Korean Peninsula. "Through multiple summit meetings, South Korea and the U.S. have confirmed their aligned policy stance toward North Korea and their commitment to coordination," Cho said during a parliamentary audit of the foreign ministry. "We have continued close consultations with the U.S. to encourage North Korea to return to dialogue and negotiations," he said, vowing continued efforts to encourage "constructive roles from China and Russia." The minister stressed the government's commitment to seeking "substantive progress" on the North Korean nuclear issue through a phased and practical approach aimed at halting, reducing and eventually dismantling its nuclear capabilities. item.title: Nuri rocket readies for 5th launch
item.description: Korea’s homegrown Nuri rocket completed preparations for liftoff on Tuesday, a day before its fifth launch, scheduled for around noon. According to the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA), Nuri arrived at the launchpad at the Naro Space Center in Goheung, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City, around 7:40 a.m. and was erected and secured at 10:30 a.m. KASA plans to hold its launch management committee around 8:45 a.m. Wednesday to finalize the launch time. Liftoff is planned between 12:23 p.m. and 1:30 p.m., with the flight expected to last about 30 minutes. The fifth launch is intended to build Nuri’s reliability through repeated production and launches using the same design, while placing its largest-ever number of satellites into orbit. Since the fourth launch last year, Hanwha Aerospace has been overseeing the production and assembly process as the rocket’s system integrator. The Nuri will carry 15 satellites on its fifth launch: five NEONSAT swarm microsatellites as the primary payload and 10 CubeSats as secondary payloads. The total payload weight is about 1,071 kilogra

item.title: Gov't honors pioneers who shaped Korea's alphabet and spread it globally
item.description: Long before digital typography defined everyday communication across smartphones and computer screens in East Asia, Korea relied heavily on imported Japanese typesetting. That changed when Seok Geum-ho founded Sandoll, pioneering an industry that produced more than 1,000 distinct Korean fonts over four decades and permanently altered the visual identity of the modern written language. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Tuesday that the late font designer will posthumously receive the Eungwan Order of Cultural Merit, Korea’s top cultural honor, on Friday during the upcoming 580th Hangul Day national ceremony at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts in Seoul. The annual awards recognize eight individuals and two organizations for significant contributions to the development, research, and international growth of Hangeul, the Korean alphabet created in 1443 by King Sejong the Great to promote popular literacy. Joining Seok among top honorees is Baek Tae-hyeon, vice president of Korean Institute in Central Asia, who will receive the Okgwan Order of Cultural Merit. Baek s

item.title: Actor Park Bo-gum turns palace sounds into new Korean travel experience
item.description: Actor Park Bo-gum led a group of roughly 100 international visitors on a soundscape walking tour at Changgyeong Palace earlier this month, spearheading a campaign by cultural authorities to shift tourism promotion toward sensory travel. Organized by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism alongside the Korea Tourism Organization, the "Korea Sound Journey" event brought together travelers and content creators selected from more than 2,300 applicants across 20 countries, including the United States, China, Japan and Thailand. The initiative directly expands on the country's 2026 global advertising campaign, "Begin to Hear Korea," which launched in July. Starring Park — serving his second consecutive year as Korea's honorary tourism ambassador — the promotional series features the actor alongside a Danish musician traveling across the peninsula to record intimate, everyday soundscapes. item.title: Foreign visitors to Seoul up 22% through August
item.description: The number of foreign visitors to Seoul in the first eight months of this year increased by about 22 percent from the same period last year, while their credit card spending in the city surged nearly 60 percent, data from the city government showed Tuesday. Seoul attracted a record 11.56 million foreign tourists in the January to August period, up 21.6 percent from a year earlier, the government said, noting their credit card spending surged 59.9 percent year-on-year to 7.78 trillion won ($5.8 billion). In August alone, 1.72 million foreign visitors visited the capital, up 23.3 percent from 1.4 million a year earlier, it noted. By country, tourists from China, Japan and Taiwan accounted for 66.4 percent of foreign visitors to Seoul in August. China topped the list with 636,000 visitors (36.9 percent), followed by Japan with 322,000 (18.6 percent) and Taiwan with 188,000 (10.9 percent). item.title: Defense chief says mine-removal operation a 'decisive' response against N. Korea
item.description: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said Tuesday the mine-clearing operation conducted at the site of a recent blast inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) was a "decisive" response against North Korea, noting it marked the first such mission inside the buffer zone between the two Koreas. Kang made the remarks a day after the South Korean military announced the final result of a joint investigation with the U.N. Command (UNC) into the Sept. 21 mine blast that left three South Korean soldiers injured. The joint probe concluded that antipersonnel mines deliberately planted by North Korean troops south of the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) were the cause of the explosion. "(Such a mine-clearing operation) is unprecedented in history," Kang told reporters at the defense ministry compound. "I believe (the operation) was a decisive response (on our side)," he added. The defense chief brushed aside allegations that the South Korean military's response was too "passive" and "defensive," saying it had taken necessary measures by removing the land mines from the DMZ on Monday. item.title: Former press secretary Karoline Leavitt lands her next gig: Fox News contributor
item.description: NEW YORK — Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt has found her next chapter: She is heading to Fox News. Leavitt will serve as an on-air contributor beginning Nov. 1, the network said Monday. “Karoline’s firsthand experience in the White House and on the presidential campaign trail gives her a distinct understanding of today’s political landscape,” said the network’s CEO, Suzanne Scott. For her part, Leavitt, in the same statement, said she looked forward “to bringing my unique perspective from my experience as White House Press Secretary, along with the same energy and candor that defined my tenure, to Fox’s millions of viewers across their many platforms.” Leavitt, now 29, was the youngest person to hold the role of press secretary. When she left at the end of August, President Donald Trump described her as one of his “most trusted aides.” At the time she said she wanted to spend more time with her two children. Her second child, Viviana, was born in May, and she has a two-year-old son. Leavitt is not the first of Trump's press secretaries to join Fox

item.title: MiCo chairman wins top US ceramic industry award
item.description: MiCo Group Chairman Jeon Seon-kyu has received a top honor from the American Ceramic Society (ACerS) for his leadership in advancing ceramic technology, the company said Tuesday. Jeon was presented with the Medal for Leadership in the Advancement of Ceramic Technology at ACerS’ Annual Honors & Awards Banquet on Monday (local time) in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The award recognizes senior industry executives who have demonstrated leadership and vision in driving corporate growth and advancing the ceramic industry. Up to two recipients are selected each year, one from the Americas and one from outside the region. Jeon was the sole recipient this year. Jeon is the first Korean to receive the award. In Asia, only four Japanese and two Chinese recipients have previously been selected. ACerS recognized Jeon for MiCo Group’s development of advanced ceramic technologies used at major semiconductor manufacturing sites worldwide. It also highlighted the group’s efforts to develop core ceramic materials, localize key components for semiconductor manufacturing equipment and establish mass-produc

item.title: Hearts2Hearts releases Korean version of Japanese debut single 'Iconic Heart'
item.description: Girl group Hearts2Hearts released a Korean-language version of "Iconic Heart," the title track of its first Japanese single, on Monday, its agency SM Entertainment said. "Iconic Heart (Korean Ver.)" is available on major streaming platforms, about two months after the original came out in Japan on Aug. 12. The song is a dance track inspired by Jersey club, a fast-paced style of club music that originated in the U.S. state of New Jersey, and is built around bright synthesizers and bouncy beats. Its lyrics convey the excitement of moving forward together through playful, youthful imagery, according to SM, one of Korea's largest K-pop agencies and home to acts such as aespa and NCT. The agency said the Korean version offers a new take on the track while keeping the energy of the original. The group first performed the Korean version Friday at Spotify Closer, a concert held in partnership with the music streaming service in Seoul's Yeongdeungpo District. Spotify launched the series to spotlight Korean artists. Hearts2Hearts was its first featured act. Hearts2Hearts plans to promote the single

item.title: 'I Live Alone' viewers captivated by actor who lives in 90-year-old home
item.description: Actor Kim Min has won praise from viewers after revealing his unconventional daily life and personal philosophy on MBC's reality show "I Live Alone." Beyond the intensity he has shown in acting roles, Kim displayed a free-spirited side as he filled his days with home repairs, martial arts and hands-on projects. But it was his outlook on life — particularly his belief that being "cool" comes from how a person spends their time rather than their looks — that resonated most with viewers. The Oct. 2 episode of "I Live Alone" offered a glimpse into Kim's life in Dongducheon, Gyeonggi Province, where he has lived alone for 28 years. He resides in a roughly 90-year-old house whose distinctive atmosphere and unconventional setup immediately drew attention. Kim began his day by running a generator for electricity and tearing into an entire baguette. He repaired a damaged floor himself with cement, worked on woodworking projects and practiced martial arts. Despite living in surroundings that might seem inconvenient to others, Kim appeared perfectly at ease, making and repairing what he needed

item.title: Sogang University selected for government-led AI training project
item.description: Sogang University is stepping up efforts to foster professionals capable of driving the artificial intelligence (AI) transformation of the manufacturing industry under a government-led initiative. The university said it has been selected for the AI innovation skills development project, which is promoted by the Ministry of Science and ICT and administered by the Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation (IITP). Cho Sung-in, a professor in the university’s Department of Artificial Intelligence, will lead the project. Under the project, the university will receive 16.25 billion won ($12 million) in government funding over five years and five months through December 2031. The university plans to nurture master’s- and doctoral-level students capable of understanding manufacturing processes and developing AI models, as well as applying and validating them in industrial settings. A university official said the project calls for nurturing AI transformation students capable of shaping the future of Korea’s manufacturing industry through cyber-physical proces

item.title: KickFlip takes bold step forward with 'Kick Off The Wall'
item.description: Emerging K-pop powerhouse KickFlip is shedding its "rookie" label to step onto the global stage. Returning from a six-month hiatus, all seven members took a hands-on approach to their new mini-album, "KICK OFF THE WALL Pt. 1." Anchored by a feature from American singer-songwriter iann dior on the title track, "Kick Off The Wall," alongside co-lead "Incomplete," the release delivers a story of confronting uncertainty and forging your own path. Packed with energetic performances, personal songwriting and a bold crossover sound, KickFlip is betting on its most ambitious project yet to prove its reach extends far beyond Korea. To dig deeper into how this new direction came together, the band sat down to discuss the creative journey behind the music. Q. You are returning about six months after “My First Kick,” so how do you feel about this comeback? KickFlip: We’re excited to show many new sides of ourselves, starting with our first double title tracks, and we’re looking forward to sharing the album with everyone. Q. What story did you want to tell through “KICK OFF THE WALL Pt. 1”

item.title: Finance minister vows efforts to tame inflation, boost growth
item.description: Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il on Tuesday vowed to focus on taming inflation to ease the cost-of-living burden while boosting economic growth through major government-led initiatives, including the three megaprojects. Lee made the remarks during a parliamentary audit by the finance, economy, planning and budget committee at the National Assembly, stressing his priorities are aimed at improving people's livelihoods and addressing economic disparities. It was Lee's first parliamentary audit session since taking office last month. "We will maintain consumer price stability, which is the foundation of people's livelihoods," the policymaker said. Lee added the finance ministry will focus particularly on stabilizing the prices of everyday necessities, such as fuel and food. "We will take stern action against irregular activities disrupting market prices and make efforts to ease the financial burdens on vulnerable groups," Lee said. item.title: Watchdog unveils guidelines on deceptive 'dark patterns' on online platforms
item.description: Korea's fair trade watchdog on Tuesday released guidelines for online platforms to avoid "dark patterns," or deceptive practices designed to make it difficult for users to cancel subscriptions or induce them to make irrational purchases. The Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said the latest guidelines consolidate and update existing guidance and provide detailed examples of violations to help platform operators comply with the rules. Dark patterns refer to practices that trick consumers into making payments or signing up for services without fully understanding what they are agreeing to. Examples include enrolling consumers in monthly subscription services without their knowledge or making cancellations difficult. Under the guidelines, platform operators are advised to place cancellation links in easily accessible locations, such as the website's homepage or sections accessible from it, including "My Account," rather than in less intuitive locations, such as "Security Settings." The FTC advised platform operators against automatically adding options consumers have not explicitly selected durin

item.title: Nat'l Assembly kicks off annual audit of gov't agencies
item.description: The National Assembly launched its annual audit of government agencies Tuesday, with rival parties clashing over the Supreme Court chief's refusal to recommend a new justice nominee to the president and the recently publicized transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) from Ukraine. Eight of the Assembly's 17 standing committees opened their sessions starting at 10 a.m. on the first day of the audit, scheduled to run through Oct. 27. During the audit of the legislation and judiciary committee, lawmakers mainly wrangled over Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae's refusal to recommend a new candidate for court justice as requested by the presidential office. Earlier in August, the presidential office asked Cho to recommend a new candidate after taking issue with his written recommendation of two Supreme Court justice nominees to President Lee Jae Myung. Cho rejected the request, citing a lack of constitutional grounds to do so. item.title: US warns foreign financial institutions not to do business with Iran
item.description: WASHINGTON — The United States on Monday warned foreign financial institutions that if they conducted any business with Iran or its banking sector they could be sanctioned by Washington. "Foreign financial institutions continuing to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could be targeted at any time without advance notification and should take immediate action to terminate such activity and relationships," the US Treasury said in an "alert" statement. The United States launched its war against Iran in late February, killing the country's leadership and demanding it cease any nuclear-related activities. The war has plunged the Middle East into violence, with Tehran's retaliatory action targeting Washington's Gulf allies and sending global energy and fertilizer prices skyrocketing after it virtually shut a key trading route. Since late August, Washington has stepped up its campaign to economically isolate Tehran, warning its allies that they would be hit by secondary sanctions if they continued to conduct transactions with the country's government. item.title: PM calls for sweeping overhaul of information security systems following wave of cyberattacks
item.description: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook called Tuesday for a sweeping overhaul of the country's information protection system, warning that recent cyberattacks on major financial institutions show that current security measures are no longer effective. Several financial firms suffered back-to-back leaks of customer information in the recent attacks, including on Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank. President Lee Jae Myung has said the issue should be taken seriously and called for a thorough investigation. On Tuesday, the prime minister presided over a meeting with related ministers to discuss the issue. "This is a serious situation because this incident is believed to have taken advantage of artificial intelligence, and if AI is used in phishing attacks, it could lead to secondary damage," Han said. "It is also a serious situation in that similar hacking methods could spread beyond the financial sector to industries, as well as government and public sectors." item.title: Police launch probe into recent cyber attacks at financial firms
item.description: Police have launched an investigation into a recent series of cyber attacks against financial companies, officials said Tuesday. Several financial companies, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank, suffered back-to-back leaks of customer information in recent hacking attacks. The National Office of Investigation (NOI) said it has formed a 28-member team to investigate the case on suspicion of violations of the information and communications network law. Officials are also reviewing whether the case should be sent to the newly launched Serious Crime Investigation Agency, which handles cyber crimes against key state facilities and hacks into electronic financial infrastructure. "(We) will carry out an investigation swiftly and strictly while closely cooperating with relevant agencies to ease the public's anxiety," the NOI said.

item.title: N. Korea reviews Q3 economy, discusses yearly goals in Cabinet meeting
item.description: North Korea has held an enlarged Cabinet meeting via video conference to review its third-quarter economic performances, state media reported Tuesday. The meeting, presided over by Premier Pak Thae-song on Monday, also discussed ways to meet the year's economic targets, according to the Rodong Sinmun, the country's most widely read state newspaper. Officials reviewed the key goals set at the Ninth Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea, held in February, which laid out a new five-year plan through 2030 that stressed economic growth and self-reliance. According to the report, Vice Premier Kim Tok-hun said, "Remarkable progress has been made, and the foundation for self-reliant economy has been reinforced." He also called on officials to shed a "passive and risk-averse" work attitude to overcome "defects and bias" found in carrying out economic policy. The meeting, in particular, called for production drives in electricity, coal, agriculture and construction. item.title: Seoul shares end lower on tech losses amid rising bond yields
item.description: Seoul shares ended lower Tuesday, led by declines in technology stocks, amid concerns over rising bond yields at multidecade highs. The Korean won rose against the U.S. dollar. After opening higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) turned lower to close down 62.35 points, or 0.89 percent, at 6,941.39. Trade volume was light at 257.27 million shares worth 19.1 trillion won ($14.2 billion), with decliners outnumbering gainers 459 to 424. Foreigners and institutions sold a net 1.75 trillion won and 1.98 billion won worth of stocks, respectively. Individuals bought a net 740.56 billion won. Investors now await third-quarter corporate earnings, with higher interest rates, elevated energy costs and renewed inflation worries pushing up global bond yields. Investors are expected to remain cautious until there is a fresh policy catalyst or strong corporate earnings results, analysts said. In Seoul, tech stocks led the decline. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics fell 1.45 percent to 272,000 won, and its chipmaking rival SK hynix declined 3.69 percent to 1.77 million won. Kore

item.title: Busan film fest kicks off with 'A-list' status for 1st time
item.description: BUSAN — The 31st edition of the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) begins its 10-day run Tuesday, with the festival seeking to bolster its global presence with its first "A-list" accreditation by a prominent global organization of filmmakers. This year's event will run through Oct. 15 in the southeastern South Korean city of Busan with 247 official selections from 59 nations, which marks the biggest slate since 2019, according to organizers. Of the total, 95 films will have their world premieres at BIFF. It marks the first time the event is taking place after the International Federation of Film Producers Associations selected BIFF as one of its 17 A-list festivals, alongside prestigious film fests, such as Cannes, Berlin and Venice. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has also added BIFF to the list of six film fests where the top winner of the Busan Award will be eligible for submission to the Oscars in the Best International Feature Film category. item.title: Hyosung Chairman Cho Hyun-Joon completes bio-spandex base in Vietnam
item.description: Hyosung TNC, the world’s largest spandex maker by market share, has launched an integrated production system in Vietnam connecting sugarcane-based bio materials to finished textile products. The investment, carried out under the leadership of Hyosung Chairman Cho Hyun-joon, is aimed at reducing reliance on fossil fuel-based raw materials while internalizing the entire supply chain, from raw materials to finished products, to strengthen the company’s presence in the global sustainable textile market. Hyosung TNC said it recently began commercial operations at its Bio-Butanediol plant in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, with an annual production capacity of 50,000 tons. Backed by a total investment of $1 billion, the facility can expand its annual production capacity to 200,000 tons depending on future market growth. BDO is a raw material used in spandex production and has traditionally been produced using petrochemical resources such as coal. item.title: 'Yoon trauma' shapes battle over new investigative chief
item.description: The row over Kim Ji-yong’s nomination as the first head of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency (SCIA) ostensibly centers on his record as a prosecutor, including allegations that he was aligned with Yoon Suk Yeol, a former prosecutor-turned-president. But the deeper issue may be anxiety within the ruling camp that the new investigative body, despite being created to separate investigation from prosecution, could operate beyond the government’s control and give rise to another Yoon-like political figure. That concern is rooted in the political aftershock of Yoon’s rise. As prosecutor general under the liberal Moon Jae-in government, he gained national prominence through investigations involving figures close to the president. That concern is rooted in the political aftershock of Yoon’s rise. As prosecutor general under the liberal Moon Jae-in government, he gained national prominence through investigations involving figures close to the president. item.title: Lawsuit accuses Starbucks of mislabeling 8 'sugar-free' protein drinks
item.description: Starbucks is facing a consumer lawsuit over claims that the protein drinks labeled “sugar-free” on its cafe menus may actually contain more sugar than a Reese’s peanut butter cup. The federal lawsuit filed late Friday in Seattle alleges that eight protein beverages Starbucks sells in the U.S. contain varying amounts of sugar even though the company lists them as sugarless. On Monday, the menu on Starbucks' U.S. website listed a 16-ounce (0.5-liter) Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha with 16 grams of sugar and a 20-ounce (0.6-liter) version of the same drink with 21 grams of sugar. By comparison, one Reese’s cup has 11 grams of sugar. Hagens Berman, a law firm that specializes in class action cases, filed the suit on behalf of three individual consumers who bought Starbucks’ sugar-free protein drinks in California, New York and Washington. “Consumers avoid sugar for various reasons, whether that be general health, diabetes and blood glucose levels or other factors, and for many, a staunch mislabeling like this is significant,” said Steve Berman, a co-founder and managing part

item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Monday the United States and South Korea still need to "work out" details of a proposed liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Alaska, while expressing confidence that the project will ultimately move forward amid strong Asian demand for American gas. "The pipeline is something that we really want to see happen and a lot of our Asian friends want to happen as well," Vance said, according to a White House pool report. "It's not just the South Koreans. The Japanese would love to see this pipeline." "So I think it's something that's going to happen," he said. "Obviously, you still got to work out some of the details and the South Koreans, you know, have spoken to that." Vance said East Asian economies that have faced higher natural gas prices would benefit from increased supplies of U.S. gas. "When there's a demand for this stuff and there really is strong demand for American natural gas, I think we're going to be able to get it done," he added. item.title: Iran president says talks with US 'meaningless': state media
item.description: TEHRAN — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that negotiations with the United States were "meaningless" and only resulted in renewed attacks, state media reported, with progress on ending the Middle East war stalled for months. "So far, they have attacked us three times after talks, and this shows that they are not seeking dialogue; rather, their goal is to overthrow the Islamic Republic of Iran," Pezeshkian was quoted as saying by the state news agency IRNA. "With an enemy that every day resorts to assassination, sanctions, pressure and threats, and that breaks its commitments, negotiations are meaningless." The Middle East war was started in late February by the U.S. and Israel when they launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, even as Washington and Tehran were in the midst of negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme. The warring parties agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution to the conflict, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz prompted a return to U.S. military operations. Negotiations

item.title: 'Reckless' AI firms can't control models, says whistleblower
item.description: NEW YORK — Leading artificial intelligence companies do not know how to keep AI systems from pursuing objectives their developers did not assign, whistleblower Jacob Coxon, a former OpenAI and Anthropic employee, warned Monday. "Companies are being extremely reckless given the stakes," Coxon told local lawmakers at a hearing before the New York City Council. In early September, the British researcher published a statement on X explaining his decision to resign from Anthropic, saying AI developers sincerely believed the technology could "kill us all by the end of the decade." His testimony made headlines around the world, and several current and former employees of AI's major players have since voiced similar concerns. While AI could bring "tremendous benefits" to society, "on the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control of these AIs and could end in human extinction," he said Monday. "We don't know how to prevent them from developing goals of their own," beyond their creators' control, Coxon explained, "and we don't have the safeguards to prevent them

item.title: Mexico sends troops after US says shots fired across border
item.description: MEXICO CITY — Mexico has deployed 500 soldiers to its border with Texas after the United States reported U.S. personnel coming under gunfire, President Claudia Sheinbaum said Monday. The troops were posted in Tamaulipas state in an area wher the rival Northeast and Gulf drug cartels are fighting for control. The United States classified both as foreign terrorist organizations in February 2025. In her routine morning press conference, Sheinbaum said the United States reported that it took "shots from the Mexican border." But she added that the Trump administration provided no evidence. Mexico offered a troop deployment anyway along the Rio Grande, she said. U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson wrote on X that U.S. Coast Guard personnel "were fired upon." He said the newly deployed Mexican troops will communicate directly with U.S. forces. "Together, we intend to patrol both sides of our shared border, protect our communities, and make it more difficult for criminal and terrorist organizations to operate," Johnson wrote. item.title: Ex-USFK commander warns time-based OPCON transfer could weaken deterrence against N. Korea
item.description: WASHINGTON — A former commander of U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) warned Monday that hastening the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) to South Korea by setting an arbitrary timeline could increase security risks and weaken the allies' deterrence capabilities against North Korea. Retired Gen. Robert Abrams, who led USFK from 2018-21, made the remarks during a webinar hosted by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies, as he discussed the allies' long-running efforts to transfer wartime OPCON from Washington to Seoul. "From my perspective and experience, I think there's a lot of risk that hasn't been properly been explained to everyone about hastening this (OPCON transfer) and putting it on a timeline," Abrams said. "Time-based fundamentally just increases risk and the risk is because there's still going to be operational shortfalls on the ROK military side," Abrams said, referring to South Korea by the acronym of its official name, the Republic of Korea. Abrams stressed that Seoul and Washington "need to make sure that we have sufficient force and capab

item.title: Students protest Cornell's response to gang rape complaint
item.description: ITHACA, New York — Cornell students thronged a campus plaza to protest the university's response to allegations of sexual assault at a fraternity house, and the school's main administration building was splashed with graffiti and damaged overnight. At a demonstration that overflowed the large space in front of the school's student center, students, faculty members and others wore purple ribbons and held signs with such messages as “support survivors, expel rapists” and “Justice 4 every Jane Doe" — the name by which the woman who reported the assault is known in court papers. Others watched from pathways, windows, and a nearby hill. “Too often, we are met with silence, we are met with statements, we are met with procedures, but not enough support,” student Athena Holloway told the crowd. “How much does it take for our university to stand with survivors?” Hispanic studies professor Julia Chang added to applause: “Rape should not be inevitable.” Speakers faulted fraternities, the university trustees and Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff, saying he and his administrat

item.title: Former press secretary Karoline Leavitt lands her next gig: Fox News contributor
item.description: NEW YORK — Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt has found her next chapter: She is heading to Fox News. Leavitt will serve as an on-air contributor beginning Nov. 1, the network said Monday. “Karoline’s firsthand experience in the White House and on the presidential campaign trail gives her a distinct understanding of today’s political landscape,” said the network’s CEO, Suzanne Scott. For her part, Leavitt, in the same statement, said she looked forward “to bringing my unique perspective from my experience as White House Press Secretary, along with the same energy and candor that defined my tenure, to Fox’s millions of viewers across their many platforms.” Leavitt, now 29, was the youngest person to hold the role of press secretary. When she left at the end of August, President Donald Trump described her as one of his “most trusted aides.” At the time she said she wanted to spend more time with her two children. Her second child, Viviana, was born in May, and she has a two-year-old son. Leavitt is not the first of Trump's press secretaries to join Fox

item.title: Nasdaq hits record high as investors focus on earnings
item.description: The Nasdaq hit an all-time high on Monday, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, as investors focused on a dip in oil prices and looked ahead to quarterly earnings reports. It was the Nasdaq's second straight intraday record high after weaker-than-expected jobs data on Friday dampened expectations for an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting this month. The S&P 500 climbed and was about 0.5 percent below its intraday record high on August 13. AI heavyweight Nvidia rose 1.6 percent, while Microsoft added 1.5 percent. Meta Platforms added 2.1 percent and Tesla climbed 2.5 percent. Oil prices slipped after crude exports from the Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies. "With the economic data calendar being light and earnings about a week away, investors are really groping for anything positive to glom onto, and clearly they're looking at lower energy prices," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. item.title: US to announce $150 mil. for Alaska power lines as Vance campaigns in Senate battleground
item.description: ABOARD AIR FORCE TWO — The U.S. Energy Department will announce $150 million in new funding for power lines in Alaska on Monday as Vice President JD Vance visits the state, where Republicans are fighting to hold a critical Senate seat in the November midterm elections. Vance is set to rally voters for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democrat Mary Peltola. Flipping the seat is key to the Democratic Party's strategy to take control of the U.S. Senate, and recent polls have Peltola, a former member of the U.S. House of Representatives, leading Sullivan. The energy plan is the latest in a series of economic and investment announcements President Donald Trump and his administration have highlighted ahead of the midterms amid voter concerns over the Iran war and high gasoline prices. item.title: Top diplomat Rubio says US monitoring Siberia plague institute death
item.description: WASHINGTON — The United States is closely monitoring the case involving a laboratory worker who died at a plague research institute in Siberia, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday. "We're watching and monitoring it closely," Rubio told reporters before leaving for a trip to Europe. "I don't think it's cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause just to keep an eye on it." A laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people, and the head of Russia's health watchdog to fly to the region. There were conflicting reports about how and where the laboratory worker, whose age was given as 28, had fallen ill, but the authorities said she had died of pneumonia. item.title: Russia reports worker at Siberian plague institute got pneumonia from unknown cause and died
item.description: Russian authorities have quarantined a hospital and are monitoring contacts of an employee at a plague research institute in Siberia who contracted pneumonia of an “unknown” cause. Local state TV said the woman died last week. Russian authorities said they found no evidence that her illness was caused by any of the pathogens she worked with. But the case has raised alarm in Russia after unconfirmed media reports suggested she might have died of pneumonic plague — a less common but severe form of plague that can spread from person to person. The woman worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk, southeastern Siberia. A state TV station in Irkutsk reported Monday that she died last week in a hospital in Shelekhov, a town just outside Irkutsk. The hospital has been placed under quarantine, Mayor Maxim Modin said Friday, no longer admitting or discharging patients, and its laboratory halted carrying out routine tests. The hospital's outpatient clinic kept operating as usual, he said. Anna Popova, head of Russia’s public health watchdog,

item.description: “Bad, bad, bad….” At Jajaeam Temple, nestled deep in the valleys of Soyo Mountain in Dongducheon, Gyeonggi Province, the silence was broken by “BAD,” a popular song by boy band ATEEZ. The man engrossed in popping moves, his gray Buddhist robes flying around him, was Ven. Deoksan, the temple’s abbot. He shot to fame after dancing to G-Dragon and Taeyang’s “Good Boy” at a Buddhist Expo in April and Michael Jackson’s “Billie Jean” at the Lotus Lantern Festival in May. Despite being in his 60s, his unconventional dance moves have earned him colorful nicknames such as the “G-Dragon of Buddhism,” “Deoksan Daegong” and “Michael Jack-sunim,” a play on Michael Jackson and the Korean word for monk, “sunim.” Ven. item.title: "Incredible Moment for the Borderlands": Judge Blocks Border Wall Expansion in Big Bend & West Texas
item.description:
In a victory for environmentalists and immigration rights’ advocates, a federal judge in El Paso, Texas, has blocked further border wall construction inside Big Bend National Park. “We slammed the brakes on $7 billion worth of corrupt construction contracts,” says Laiken Jordahl, a national public lands advocate with the Center for Biological Diversity, which sued to block the expansion. “We have effectively stopped construction across West Texas, and it’s incredible.”

Jordahl also responds to the Trump administration’s excavation of a 200-year-old cottonwood tree on the Arizona-Mexico border that had been protected by activists for months. “Watching those videos of them toppling this ancient tree that was very likely older than the border itself is symbolic of how DHS has treated the border region. They see our communities, our wildlife, our nature as a sacrifice zone,” says Jordahl.

item.title: Ebola Death Toll in DRC Tops 4,000; Trump USAID Cuts Fuel Outbreak
item.description:
We go to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the site of the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Health authorities believe the outbreak first began in January but was not detected until May, in part due to cuts in global health investments, like the dismantling of USAID. Since then, over 8,000 cases have been recorded, with more than 4,000 fatalities so far. From Bunia, Ituri province, the epicenter of the outbreak, we speak to Congolese journalist Akilimali Chomachoma. Chomachoma describes the strain on the underfunded Congolese healthcare system as the disease spreads. Many frontline workers have not been paid for months.

“We are seeing this outbreak emerge, and really unfurl, in a setting of decreased global health support,” says Craig Spencer, a doctor and public health expert based in the United States who contracted Ebola while on a medical mission to Guinea in 2014. “The U.S. has not shown up in the same way that it has in previous Ebola outbreaks.” Spencer also comments on the “unprecedented” measles outbreak in the United States, which he warns is likely to continue and lead to additional deaths.

item.title: French High School Students Lead Mass Protests over School Funding, Inequality; Thousands Arrested
item.description:
Nearly 2,000 French high schools are blockaded or closed today amid massive student-led protests over school funding and inequality. The demonstrations began in September at a single school in the economically deprived suburbs of Paris, where students protested teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and dilapidated school buildings beset by rats, falling debris and more. But the scope of the protests has widened amid a violent crackdown by French police. French authorities have arrested more than 5,000 people, largely underage students, since the movement began. Violent police tactics have led to serious injuries. One protester lost an eye after being hit by a rubber bullet, while another lost a hand when he picked up a police stun grenade.

We hear from an anonymous protester who describes the violence meted out on students, who “aren’t even adults yet,” and from Claire Vigneau, general secretary of Fédération Syndicale Étudiante, the French student union, who reports from a protest in Rennes, Brittany, “where we are trying to escape from the policemen that are chasing us with tear gas and with water cannon[s].”

“The amount of spending that France has done on education has stagnated, if not declined,” explains French American journalist Cole Stangler. “The critiques that high school students are making are actually very similar to what teachers’ unions have been saying for quite some time.”

“Everyone is deeply, deeply angry. We are completely fed up [with] the living conditions, the school conditions, the work conditions that we have,” says Alys Rowlands, a university student in Lille and also a member of Fédération Syndicale Étudiante. “The true violence is the violence of the state that we are being faced with all day, every day, all year. That’s the true violence: having no money, having difficulty finishing the month, having less and less help from the state, having to choose between eating and putting your heating on during the winter.”

item.title: From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach
item.description: Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected. Behind those warning signs is an El Niño whose Pacific Ocean temperatures have already surpassed the equivalent measurements during the historic 1997 and 2015 events – part of an unfolding climate pattern being dubbed a “Super El Niño” by some climate watchers.

item.title: What U.S. Supreme Court judges said at a hearing on climate damages from oil and gas
